items.title: US Embassy explains how Ghanaians can secure emergency visa interviews
items.description: The United States Embassy in Accra has outlined the procedure for nonimmigrant visa applicants seeking an earlier interview because of an unexpected emergency, urging them to follow the required steps and provide evidence to support their requests. The provision is intended for people whose circumstances may require urgent travel to the United States, including those seeking emergency medical attention or travelling to attend the funeral of a family member, an update on Friday, October 6, explained. The Embassy’s guidance also identifies urgent, unforeseen business needs as a possible basis for consideration. However, applicants have been cautioned that expedited interview slots are limited and that submitting a request does not guarantee an earlier appointment or an interview before the intended travel date. Individuals seeking to travel to the U.S. urgently may qualify for an expedited visa appointment if the intended travel is for: • Emergency medical care or bereavement (death of a family member) • Urgent, unanticipated business When making a request, it is ESSENTIAL to provide a justification explaining your circumstances in detail as well as any relevant documents. There is a very limited number of expedited appointments available, and the Embassy cannot guarantee an interview prior to the planned travel date. Learn more on our website: https://t.co/N4V7DXsYTO — U.S. Embassy Accra (@USEmbassyGhana) November 6, 2026 Applicants must first complete the online Nonimmigrant Visa Application Form, known as the DS-160, pay the applicable visa fee and book the earliest available regular interview through the official appointment portal, usvisaappt.com. Only after completing these requirements can they ask the Consular Section to consider an emergency appointment. How to apply To submit a request, applicants must sign in to their account on the appointment portal, go to “My Dashboard” and select “Create Emergency Request”. They are then required to complete an Emergency Request Form, explaining the nature of the emergency, the intended travel date and why an earlier interview is necessary. Supporting documents must also be uploaded to substantiate the claim. These may include relevant medical records or correspondence, depending on the nature of the emergency. The Embassy has stressed the importance of providing a clear and detailed explanation, together with credible documentation, to enable consular officials to assess the circumstances. An applicant whose request is approved will receive an email notification and must return to the appointment portal to select a new interview date and time from the available slots. Those whose requests are declined will also be notified by email but will retain their original interview appointments. An earlier interview does not guarantee a visa The US Department of State’s general guidance on nonimmigrant visas makes clear that expedited appointments are considered for urgent and unforeseen circumstances, including medical emergencies, funerals and certain school start dates. Applicants must provide evidence of their need for an earlier interview. It also cautions that requests to travel for weddings, graduation ceremonies, last-minute tourism or annual business and professional conferences do not ordinarily meet the emergency criteria. Applicants travelling for such purposes are advised to apply through the regular process well ahead of their intended departure. Even where an expedited appointment is granted, applicants must still satisfy all the requirements for the visa category for which they are applying. The decision to issue or refuse a visa is made separately by a consular officer after the application has been assessed. The Department of State also advises applicants to plan their journeys early, as interview waiting periods can change depending on demand and staffing levels. Applicants are further advised to review the Embassy’s security instructions and list of prohibited items before attending their interviews. Once passports or other documents are ready for release, applicants will be notified and given instructions on how to register for collection. The Embassy does not permit applicants to collect their passports or documents personally from its premises.

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le roi Gan déclaré officiellement mort 4 ans après son enlèvement
items.description: Après plus de quatre années sans nouvelles de leur souverain, les sages de la cour royale d’Obiré ont annoncé son décès, ce jeudi 5 novembre 2026. Les rites funéraires ont débuté dans la soirée, tandis que les grandes funérailles sont prévues dans trois mois. La communauté gan est désormais fixée sur le sort de son roi. Les sages de la cour royale d’Obiré ont officiellement annoncé, ce jeudi 5 novembre 2026, le décès du souverain, enlevé le 27 septembre 2022 avec son fils alors qu’ils revenaient du champ. Depuis cet enlèvement, aucune nouvelle du roi n’avait été rendue publique. Selon les informations rapportées par Bafuji Info, les sages de la cour royale étaient informés de son décès et préparaient, dans la discrétion, son annonce ainsi que les rites coutumiers qui l’accompagnent. Cette déclaration officielle met fin à plus de quatre années d’incertitude autour du sort du souverain. Les rites funéraires débutent à Obiré L’annonce ouvre une période de deuil au sein de la communauté gan. Les premières cérémonies funéraires ont commencé dans la soirée du 5 novembre et doivent se poursuivre pendant quelques jours. Les grandes funérailles sont, quant à elles, annoncées dans trois mois. La désignation et l’intronisation d’un nouveau roi interviendront après cette étape, conformément au processus coutumier. Un enlèvement survenu dans un contexte sécuritaire tendu Situé à environ 11 kilomètres de la commune rurale de Loropéni, dans la province du Poni, région du Djôrô, le village d’Obiré avait été profondément marqué par l’enlèvement de son souverain et de son fils. Cet événement était intervenu dans un contexte sécuritaire particulièrement difficile. Dès août 2022, la menace terroriste s’était accentuée dans la zone de Loropéni, alimentant notamment des tensions communautaires. Dans un communiqué publié le 14 août 2022, le gouverneur du Sud-Ouest de l’époque, Boureima Savadogo, avait appelé les populations à éviter la stigmatisation et les amalgames. Quatre ans après la disparition de leur roi, les populations d’Obiré et l’ensemble de la communauté gan entament ainsi une nouvelle étape : celle du deuil et de l’accomplissement des rites funéraires en hommage à leur souverain. items.title: Espagne : le Parquet européen enquête sur de possibles fraudes liées à la ligne ferroviaire accidentée
items.description: Le Parquet européen a annoncé vendredi l’ouverture d’une enquête sur de possibles fraudes concernant l’utilisation de fonds européens destinés à la rénovation et à la sécurisation de la ligne ferroviaire à grande vitesse Madrid-Séville, où une collision a fait 69 morts la semaine dernière. L’enquête vise notamment à déterminer si des fonds européens consacrés à l’amélioration de la sécurité, de la signalisation et des systèmes de communication de cette ligne ont été utilisés conformément à leur destination. Des mesures d’enquête sont actuellement menées auprès d’Adif, l’entreprise publique chargée de la gestion des infrastructures ferroviaires espagnoles, ainsi que d’autres organismes publics. Le Parquet européen précise que cette procédure fait suite à des soupçons de « possible fraude affectant des fonds européens » destinés aux travaux de rénovation et d’amélioration de la sécurité du réseau. Ce n’est pas la première fois que le financement et la sécurité de cette ligne ferroviaire font l’objet de vérifications. En mars dernier, une enquête similaire avait été ouverte après un autre accident ferroviaire survenu près d’Adamuz, en Andalousie. La collision de deux trains à grande vitesse avait alors fait 46 morts. Quelques mois plus tard, un nouvel accident meurtrier est survenu à hauteur d’Urda, à environ 150 kilomètres au sud de Madrid. Deux trains à grande vitesse sont entrés en collision, faisant 69 morts. La répétition de ces accidents sur le réseau ferroviaire espagnol alimente désormais les interrogations sur l’état des infrastructures et sur la gestion des investissements destinés à renforcer leur sécurité. Dans ce contexte, le ministre espagnol des Transports, Óscar Puente, a annoncé sa démission mardi. Il était à la tête du ministère lors des deux accidents ferroviaires. L’enquête du Parquet européen devra désormais déterminer si d’éventuelles irrégularités ont affecté les fonds européens consacrés à la modernisation de la ligne Madrid-Séville. À ce stade, l’ouverture de cette procédure ne préjuge pas de l’existence de fraudes ni de la responsabilité d’éventuels acteurs. The post Espagne : le Parquet européen enquête sur de possibles fraudes liées à la ligne ferroviaire accidentée appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Nouvelles directives de la BCEAO sur les paiements instantanés: : Ce qui change pour les clients de UBA depuis le 2 novembre 2026
items.description: Le paysage des transferts d'argent et des services monétiques connaît un tournant majeur dans l'espace UEMOA. En application des nouvelles orientations réglementaires de la Banque Centrale des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (BCEAO) entrées en vigueur le 2 novembre 2026, la banque UBA Burkina a adapté l'ensemble de ses transactions interopérables à la plateforme de paiement instantané PI-SPI. Cette transition entraîne des modifications concrètes pour les usagers : suspension temporaire de la recharge des cartes prépayées via Orange Money, passage exclusif des virements « Bank to Wallet » par la nouvelle application RedPay, mais également relèvement substantiel des plafonds de recharge des cartes Visa et gratuité des transferts nationaux jusqu'à concurrence de 8 000 FCFA par jour. Décryptage d'une réforme qui redéfinit les règles du jeu bancaire. L'interopérabilité bancaire franchit une étape décisive dans la sous-région ouest-africaine. En vertu des dispositions de l'Instruction n°020 du 8 octobre 2026 et de l'Avis n°0019 du 2 octobre 2026 édictés par la BCEAO, la plateforme de paiement instantané PI-SPI devient désormais le réseau unique régissant les transferts interopérables. Conçu pour interconnecter sans intermédiaire les banques, les établissements financiers et les opérateurs de Mobile Money au sein de l'UEMOA, ce dispositif vise à standardiser les règles, à unifier la tarification et à garantir l'instantanéité des flux monétaires d'une institution à une autre. Cette harmonisation réglementaire bouleverse directement les habitudes des usagers de la banque UBA Burkina. Depuis le 2 novembre 2026, l’ensemble des opérations de transfert dites « Bank to Wallet » (du compte bancaire vers le portefeuille électronique) transitent exclusivement par la passerelle PI-SPI. Pour transférer des fonds depuis leur compte vers un portefeuille Orange Money, les clients sont désormais tenus d'utiliser l'application mobile RedPay (disponible sur Google Play et App Store), sur laquelle ils doivent créer un alias d'identification avant d'initier et de valider leurs transactions. Autre répercussion notable : la recharge directe des cartes prépayées UBA via le canal Orange Money est temporairement suspendue depuis le 2 novembre 2026 en raison des nouvelles orientations réglementaires. Pour maintenir leurs cartes actives, les clients sont invités à recourir aux canaux alternatifs maintenus par l'établissement : les guichets des agences UBA Burkina, le réseau des distributeurs agréés, le canal LEO, l’application UBA Mobile App ou encore le service d'Internet Banking. En contrepartie, la banque compense cette contrainte technique par un relèvement notable des capacités des cartes prépayées Visa : Le plafond par recharge passe du simple au double, grimpant de 2 000 000 FCFA à 4 000 000 FCFA. Le plafond mensuel cumulé est porté de 10 000 000 FCFA à 15 000 000 FCFA. L'entrée en service du réseau PI-SPI redéfinit également le barème des frais de transaction au bénéfice d'une plus grande transparence. Sur le plan national, les transferts interopérables bénéficient désormais d'une gratuité totale jusqu'à 8 000 FCFA cumulés par jour. Au-delà de ce seuil quotidien, une tarification unique fixée à 0,8 % Hors Taxes (HT) s'applique exclusivement sur la part excédentaire (à titre d'illustration, pour un virement de 20 000 FCFA dans la journée, les 8 000 premiers francs sont exemptés de frais, et les 12 000 FCFA restants sont facturés à hauteur de 96 FCFA HT) . Pour les opérations transfrontalières au sein de l'espace UEMOA, le tarif est uniforme à 0,8 % HT du montant transféré, tandis que la réception de tout transfert demeure strictement gratuite. Afin d'atténuer les frictions liées à cette mutation technologique et réglementaire, l'établissement bancaire a mis en place un dispositif d'assistance dédié. La clientèle peut s'adresser au Centre de satisfaction clientèle au numéro local (+226 25 49 35 00) ou par messagerie électronique, ainsi qu'à une permanence téléphonique opérationnelle durant les week-ends et jours fériés (+226 01 15 70 70) pour guider les utilisateurs dans l'appropriation de ces nouveaux canaux. items.title: Mutfwang: Educated Nigerians masterminding corruption, institutional decay
items.description: …says professionals behind major governance failures …challenges graduates to choose integrity over wealth By Joseph Erunke, Abuja Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has accused educated Nigerians of masterminding some of the country’s most damaging corruption scandals, financial fraud and institutional abuses, saying the nation’s governance crisis is not a result of a shortage of intellectual capacity but a failure of conscience. Mutfwang said some of the most sophisticated acts of financial fraud, contract manipulation, money laundering and subversion of public institutions were perpetrated by people whose academic qualifications and professional expertise should ordinarily be deployed for national development. The governor spoke on Friday in Abuja while delivering the convocation lecture at the 15th Convocation Ceremony of Veritas University. In his lecture titled, “Building the Nigeria We Want: The Role of the Educated Mind,” he warned that education without moral discipline had become a dangerous instrument against the country’s progress. He challenged the graduating students to rethink the purpose of university education, insisting that academic certificates and intellectual brilliance would amount to little if deployed for selfish interests at the expense of society. According to him, Nigeria’s development challenges cannot be blamed entirely on inadequate manpower or lack of expertise, as many individuals responsible for undermining public institutions are highly educated and professionally trained. Describing the situation as an uncomfortable reality the country must confront, Mutfwang said some of Nigeria’s most entrenched governance failures were products of educated minds. He said: “Indeed, I make an uncomfortable observation: the afflictions I diagnosed earlier, prebendalism, the privatisation of public office, grand corruption, the capture of institutions, are almost never the work of illiterate minds. They are overwhelmingly executed by educated minds. “The contract, the doctored account, the laundered fund, the ingenious evasion of law. All these are the signatures of trained minds. This is the paradox we must confront. The educated mind is at once our greatest hope, and when corrupted, it becomes our most sophisticated danger.” The governor also cited internet fraudsters, popularly known as Yahoo boys, as an example of intelligence deployed in the wrong direction, arguing that criminal ingenuity reflected a lack of moral restraint rather than an absence of intelligence. “The Yahoo boy is certainly not a derelict. He is a work of intelligence, but intelligence wrongly applied,” he said. Mutfwang maintained that Nigeria had no shortage of brilliant citizens, noting the achievements of Nigerians across different professions and on international platforms. However, he lamented that the country had failed to translate its abundant intellectual resources into responsible leadership, accountable governance and sustainable development. He urged the graduating students not to measure success solely by their earning capacity, professional positions or social standing, but by the extent to which their knowledge improved the lives of others. According to him, intellectual capacity must be matched with conscience, warning that an educated person without moral discipline could inflict greater damage on society than someone without formal education. “Knowledge tells you what you can do, but conscience tells you what you should do. An educated mind without a formed conscience is not an asset to any nation. It is a very efficient danger,” he declared. The governor identified integrity, responsibility and competence as three critical attributes Nigeria needed from its educated population to overcome its development challenges. He explained that responsibility required citizens to accept the consequences of their decisions rather than hide behind claims of good intentions. Citing the principles in The Ethics of Responsibility, Mutfwang said national development required individuals willing to take ownership of the outcomes of their actions. He described the Nigeria of his aspiration as a country where hospitals delivered quality healthcare, courts dispensed justice, schools provided meaningful education and public office holders regarded their positions as opportunities to serve rather than avenues for personal enrichment. “The Nigeria we want is a nation of institutions that work, where the hospital heals, where the courts deliver justice, where the schools teach, and public office serves truly the public. “It is a nation where merit is rewarded and mediocrity is not enthroned, where security is felt in the farm, in the market, at home, where prosperity is shared rather than captured, and where leaders understand office as stewardship and not as a spoil,” he said. Mutfwang, who reaffirmed his belief in Nigeria’s unity, said the country’s ethnic, linguistic and cultural diversity should be regarded as an opportunity to build a stronger nation rather than an excuse for division. He also disagreed with the notion that the 1914 amalgamation was necessarily a mistake, arguing that Nigeria’s diverse peoples had a common responsibility to determine the country’s future. “I do not share the view that the amalgamation of 1914 was necessarily a mistake. I acknowledge our extraordinary diversity and the fact that our peoples have distinct histories, distinct languages and distinct identities. Yet I believe God has a purpose for bringing us together. Our responsibility is to decide what we will make of this country,” he said. The governor further expressed concern over the withdrawal of credible and competent Nigerians from politics and public service, warning that their absence was worsening the country’s governance challenges. He urged educated Nigerians to stop abandoning the public space to individuals who might not possess the integrity and commitment required to serve the country. “One reason our public square so often disappoints is that too many good people have vacated it, abandoning it to those least fit to occupy it. “Government and public service are not dirty words. They are the arenas in which the future of a nation is decided. If the best remain outside, the worst will not,” he warned. Mutfwang stressed that nation-building was not the exclusive responsibility of elected officials or political appointees, but required the everyday commitment and responsible decisions of citizens across different professions. The post Mutfwang: Educated Nigerians masterminding corruption, institutional decay appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: APGA adopts Tinubu, flags off nationwide campaign
items.description: …Soludo cites South-East projects, urges strategic voting By Steve Oko The All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) has adopted President Bola Tinubu as its presidential candidate for the 2027 general election, with Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, saying the decision was informed by the need for progressive forces to work together. Soludo made the declaration on Friday while flagging off APGA’s nationwide election campaign at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, Anambra State, where the party unveiled more than 253 candidates contesting various elective positions across the country. The governor, who is APGA’s National Leader, said the decision to support Tinubu was consistent with the party’s political tradition, recalling that APGA had similarly adopted former President Goodluck Jonathan in the 2011 and 2015 presidential elections. He said the party’s support for Tinubu was also informed by what he described as the Federal Government’s commitment to the South-East, particularly in infrastructure development. “Today, as we unveil our campaign as the foremost progressive party in Nigeria, we are also officially adopting President Bola Tinubu as the presidential candidate of APGA. “We did it in 2011 and 2015 for President Jonathan. We are repeating it in 2027 because progressives are working together to support a President who loves Ndi Igbo and Ndi Anambra,” Soludo declared. Citing the dualisation and rehabilitation of the Enugu-Onitsha Expressway and other federal projects in the region, the governor urged voters to approach the 2027 elections with political pragmatism rather than sentiment. He said voting decisions should be guided by tangible benefits, enlightened self-interest and strategic political considerations capable of advancing the interests of the South-East. Soludo also charged APGA candidates and members to intensify grassroots mobilisation through door-to-door campaigns, assuring them that he would personally join the candidates in soliciting votes. He expressed confidence in the party’s electoral prospects, urging voters to distinguish between reason and emotion ahead of the January 16 and February 6, 2027 elections. At the event, Soludo presented party flags to 44 APGA candidates contesting legislative seats in Anambra State. The candidates comprised three senatorial candidates, 11 House of Representatives candidates and 30 State House of Assembly candidates. Earlier, APGA National Chairman, Barrister Sly Ezeokenwa, commended Soludo for what he described as transparent and competitive party primaries conducted in compliance with electoral laws. Ezeokenwa attributed the influx of new members into the party to Soludo’s people-oriented policies, describing Anambra as APGA’s political stronghold. He expressed confidence that the party would record a decisive victory in the forthcoming elections. items.title: Parkinson’s journey: Franklin Cudjoe undergoes successful surgery in the US
items.description: IMANI Africa Founding President, Franklin Cudjoe, has been discharged from the hospital following a successful surgery in the United States and says he will spend the next two weeks recovering at his apartment. In a Facebook update on Friday, October 6, Mr Cudjoe announced his return from the hospital, expressing optimism about the next phase of his treatment. “Discharged and back in my apartment. Next 2 weeks of healing and then the magic will happen,” he posted. The update comes a day after he appealed to Ghanaians and other well-wishers to pray for him as he prepared to undergo surgery at RUSH University Medical Center in Chicago. In that earlier message, he expressed confidence in the medical teams attending to him and thanked those who had helped facilitate his emergency travel and supported his treatment journey. Mr Cudjoe, who disclosed in January 2026 that he had been living with Parkinson’s disease for eight years, has been sharing updates about his condition and treatment to raise awareness of the neurological disorder. Calls for better neurological care in Ghana Ahead of the operation, the IMANI Africa president had also spoken about his desire to use the experience to draw attention to gaps in specialised neurological care in Ghana. He said that, after his surgery, he planned to host neurosurgeons and neurologists in the country to help advance access to specialist personnel, medical equipment, medicines and treatment. He also disclosed that a documentary, would chronicle his preparations and journey from Ghana to the United States for the procedure. Mr Cudjoe had earlier acknowledged the support he received from businessman Ibrahim Mahama and neurologists in Ghana but expressed concern about the limited number of specialists available to manage conditions such as Parkinson’s disease. His public disclosure of the diagnosis was intended, in part, to encourage greater awareness of the condition and support for people living with it. Parkinson’s disease is a progressive neurological disorder that affects movement. Although it has no cure, symptoms can be managed through treatment and other interventions.

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le Conseil des ministres met en place l’Agence Burkinabè de Médecine Traditionnelle
items.description: Réuni ce jeudi 5 novembre 2026 sous la présidence du Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, le Conseil des ministres a adopté plusieurs textes majeurs touchant aux secteurs minier, sanitaire et sportif. Parmi les principales décisions figurent la création de la société d’État Faso SANU, la réorganisation de l’exploitation minière artisanale et la mise en place de l’Agence burkinabè de médecine traditionnelle. Le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a présidé, ce jeudi 5 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, le Conseil des ministres hebdomadaire. À l’issue de cette session ordinaire, plusieurs dossiers et projets de textes ont été examinés et adoptés dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de la vision de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP), selon le porte-parole du Gouvernement, Gilbert Ouédraogo. Au titre du ministère de l’Énergie, des Mines et des Carrières, trois décrets ont été adoptés, avec pour objectif de mieux encadrer l’exploitation minière artisanale et de renforcer le contrôle de l’État sur ce sous-secteur. Le premier décret définit les conditions et les modalités de réorganisation des sites miniers illégaux, notamment ceux faisant l’objet de conflits ou présentant un caractère stratégique pour l’État. Selon le ministre chargé des Mines, Yacouba Zabré Gouba, cette mesure vise à assainir les sites concernés et à instaurer un climat plus apaisé pour l’exploitation artisanale de l’or. Le ministre a également rappelé que l’utilisation de la main-d’œuvre infantile sur les sites miniers sera sanctionnée conformément aux dispositions du Code minier en vigueur. Faso SANU, un nouvel outil de contrôle du secteur aurifère Autre décision importante : la création d’une société d’État dénommée « Faso SANU », qui signifie « or » en langue dioula. Cette nouvelle structure doit permettre à l’État de disposer d’un instrument technique pour accompagner la réorganisation du sous-secteur minier artisanal et assurer la mise en œuvre des orientations définies. Selon Yacouba Zabré Gouba, le capital de cette société sera réparti à parts égales entre la Société nationale des substances précieuses (SONASP), à hauteur de 50 %, et le Trésor public, pour les 50 % restants. Le troisième décret adopté porte sur les statuts de cette nouvelle société. Santé : une nouvelle architecture administrative et la valorisation de la médecine traditionnelle Dans le secteur de la santé, le Conseil des ministres a adopté un décret portant modification de l’organigramme du ministère. Cette réorganisation tient compte du nouveau découpage territorial et de la mise en place des Centres médicaux communaux (CMC). Présentée par le ministre de la Santé, Robert Lucien Jean-Claude Kargougou, cette réforme vise à adapter le fonctionnement du département aux nouvelles réalités administratives et à améliorer la mise en œuvre de la politique sanitaire nationale. Parmi les principales innovations figurent la création d’un Secrétariat général adjoint chargé notamment de la supervision des structures hospitalières et des sociétés d’État, ainsi que la mise en place de nouvelles structures spécialisées. Le dispositif prévoit notamment la création du Secrétariat permanent du Conseil national de lutte contre le Sida, les infections sexuellement transmissibles (IST), les hépatites virales et la tuberculose, ainsi que du Secrétariat technique pour l’intelligence sanitaire. Le décret consacre également la création du Faso Center for Disease Control and Prevention (Faso CDC) et de l’Agence burkinabè de médecine traditionnelle. Cette dernière structure devrait contribuer à la valorisation et à la promotion des savoirs médicinaux traditionnels du Burkina Faso. La réforme prévoit par ailleurs un renforcement de la présence des services sanitaires dans les territoires, à travers la création de directions provinciales de la Santé et de centres hospitaliers provinciaux. En contrepartie, deux structures sont appelées à disparaître : la Société de gestion d’équipements et de maintenance biomédicale (SOGEMAB) et le Secrétariat technique chargé de la multisectorialité pour la nutrition. Cette mesure s’inscrit dans une logique de rationalisation et d’amélioration de l’efficacité administrative. Sport : vers une nouvelle réglementation des activités sportives Le secteur sportif a également été au cœur des décisions de cette session. Le Conseil des ministres a adopté un projet de loi portant développement des activités sportives. Ce texte vient répondre aux insuffisances relevées dans la loi n°050 portant orientation du sport et des loisirs, adoptée en 2019. Selon la ministre des Sports, Annick Lydie Djouma Pikbougoum/Zingué Ouattara, cette relecture ambitionne de mieux structurer le secteur et de faire du sport un véritable levier de développement socioéconomique. Le nouveau cadre juridique introduit plusieurs innovations. Il prévoit notamment un renforcement de la protection sociale et salariale des sportifs, avec l’objectif de leur garantir une rémunération décente. Le texte entend également encadrer les participations des équipes nationales aux compétitions internationales, désormais subordonnées à une autorisation préalable du Gouvernement. Il prend aussi en compte le développement du sport inclusif en faveur des personnes vivant avec un handicap, tout en renforçant les dispositions relatives à la santé des athlètes et à la lutte contre le dopage. À travers ces différentes décisions, le Conseil des ministres du 5 novembre 2026 engage des réformes dans trois secteurs stratégiques : les ressources minières, la santé publique et le sport. Leur mise en œuvre devra permettre de mesurer les effets concrets de ces nouvelles orientations sur l’organisation des services publics et le développement socioéconomique du Burkina Faso. items.title: After years away, Charles Okafor ‘The Primate’ roars back in ‘Issakaba Sequel’
items.description: By Benjamin Njoku True legends never really leave. They stay etched in our hearts, commanding respect, admiration and timeless relevance. That is how filmmaker Lancelot Imasuen describes Charles Okafor, affectionately known as The Primate. Okafor, who dominated Nollywood screens in the 90s and early 2000s as one of the industry’s most prolific and popular stars, is set for a grand comeback on Wednesday, November 11, when the highly anticipated action-thriller “Issakaba: The Return” hits cinemas. The premiere promises a new dawn for Nollywood, and the return of a screen icon who has been away for several years. Announcing Okafor’s return, Lancelot said his appearance on the promotional poster was a powerful reminder of the enduring legacy of a man whose talent, commanding screen presence, versatility and remarkable contribution to Nollywood have earned him a special place in Nigerian entertainment history. “The Primate is not just an actor; he is an institution, a symbol of excellence and a distinguished custodian of a generation of Nigerian storytelling,” Lancelot said. “His remarkable ability to bring characters to life, coupled with his unmistakable presence, has left an indelible impression on audiences across generations. “Seeing him return in ”Issakaba: The Return” evokes nostalgia, excitement and admiration. It is a beautiful convergence of legacy and renewed relevance, a testament to the fact that genuine talent does not grow old, and true legends never go out of fashion. The legend returns, but the legacy never leaves!” Okafor, famed for movies like “Computer Girls (2003)”, “Sting (2006)” and “Ocean Deep (2007)”, was long rumoured to have quit acting to win souls for God. In reality, he says his long absence from the screen was simply about his preference for quality movies over quantity. items.title: Délais de paiement des EEP : 35,8 jours en moyenne en septembre
items.description: Les établissements et entreprises publics ont réglé leurs fournisseurs en 35,8 jours en moyenne au titre de septembre 2026, d’après les délais déclarés que le ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et de la Performance Publique vient de publier. Le ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et de la Performance Publique a mis en ligne les délais moyens de paiement déclarés par les établissements et entreprises publics (EEP) pour le mois de septembre 2026. Ces données sont consultables dans la rubrique de l’Observatoire des délais de paiement, sur le portail du département. Pour l’ensemble de ces établissements et entreprises, la moyenne des délais de paiement déclarés atteint 35,8 jours au titre de septembre 2026. Ce chiffre agrège les déclarations de tous les EEP : il ne renvoie pas à un organisme en particulier, mais à une moyenne établie sur l’ensemble du périmètre. Il s’agit, de surcroît, de délais déclarés, c’est-à-dire communiqués par les EEP eux-mêmes, tels que le ministère les a publiés. Cette publication revêt un caractère trimestriel. Elle s’inscrit dans la démarche progressive engagée par le ministère de l’Économie et des Finances depuis la première publication, réalisée le 31 octobre 2019. La diffusion des délais de paiement des EEP ne relève donc pas d’une initiative ponctuelle : elle prolonge un exercice qui court depuis plus de sept ans, au rythme d’une publication par trimestre. Cette démarche est menée conformément aux dispositions de la Circulaire n°1632/19/DEPP du 21 juin 2019. Ce texte est relatif au renforcement et à l’accélération des mesures visant l’amélioration des délais de paiement des EEP. Il fixe ainsi l’objectif qui sous-tend les publications de l’Observatoire : améliorer le temps que mettent ces établissements et entreprises à régler leurs créanciers. La première publication, le 31 octobre 2019, est intervenue quelques mois après la signature de cette circulaire. Depuis, les délais déclarés par les EEP sont rendus publics sur le portail du ministère, où figurent aujourd’hui ceux de septembre 2026. Le dispositif repose ainsi sur trois éléments. Le premier est la déclaration des délais par les établissements et entreprises publics eux-mêmes. Le deuxième est leur mise en ligne sur le portail du ministère, dans la rubrique de l’Observatoire des délais de paiement. Le troisième est un rythme trimestriel, qui permet de suivre l’évolution de la moyenne d’une publication à l’autre. Le chiffre rendu public porte sur le seul mois de septembre 2026. Il est celui que le ministère retient comme moyenne des délais de paiement déclarés par l’ensemble des établissements et entreprises publics : 35,8 jours, calculés sur la base des déclarations de ces derniers. L’Observatoire des délais de paiement, qui héberge ces données sur le portail du ministère de l’Économie et des Finances, constitue le point d’accès où sont publiées, de manière régulière, les moyennes déclarées par les EEP. C’est dans cette rubrique que le public peut consulter les chiffres relatifs à septembre 2026, comme ceux des publications antérieures diffusées selon la même logique. The post Délais de paiement des EEP : 35,8 jours en moyenne en septembre appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: KP to introduce mobile drug testing labs
items.description: PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa will introduce five advanced mobile drug screening laboratories next week to strengthen the monitoring of medicines and detect substandard, counterfeit and suspicious drugs in markets across the province. Adviser to the governor on health and population Nigar Johar Khan reviewed the newly equipped laboratory vans during her visit to the Directorate General of Drug Control and Pharmacy Services on Friday. The five mobile laboratories will be formally inaugurated at Governor House next Tuesday. During the visit, the adviser inspected various sections of the directorate and received a briefing on its regulatory functions, drug quality monitoring and measures to ensure the availability of safe medicines. Officials said the mobile laboratories were equipped with modern Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) and Raman technologies to conduct preliminary on-site testing of medicines, including their chemical composition, ingredients and conformity with prescribed strength standards. The vans will be deployed across different divisions of the province, enabling drug inspectors to examine medicines in markets and other locations. If the initial screening identifies suspicious or substandard medicines, inspectors will collect samples and send them to the Drug Testing Laboratory in Peshawar for detailed analysis and further action. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: New state lounge planned at Islamabad airport ahead of SCO summit
items.description: RAWALPINDI: The Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) has initiated construction of a new State Lounge at Islamabad International Airport as part of Pakistan’s preparations for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit scheduled to be hosted in Islamabad in August 2027. Defence Minister Khawaja Mohammad Asif performed the groundbreaking for the new lounge. The ceremony was attended by Secretary Defence Mohammad Ali, PAA Director General AVM Mohammad Shahid Afzaal and senior officials from the Ministry of Defence and the PAA. In his welcome address, the PAA Director General highlighted the significance of the project in strengthening state protocol and hospitality arrangements at the IIA , particularly ahead of the forthcoming SCO Council of Heads of State Summit. Following the groundbreaking, the defence minister unveiled the commemorative plaque and participated in a tree plantation activity, reaffirming the commitment to environmental sustainability. The new State Lounge forms part of Pakistan’s preparations for the SCO Summit, scheduled to be hosted in Islamabad in August 2027. The facility will enhance protocol, hospitality and facilitation arrangements for visiting heads of state, foreign dignitaries, senior government officials and international delegations. Meanwhile, Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) management has started deep cleaning its fleet of aircraft in an effort to significantly improve cabin maintenance and aircraft cleanliness. A PIA spokesman said on Friday that the airline’s management had launched a deep-cleaning exercise for aircraft in its fleet. PIA has decided to focus on further improving the quality of aircraft cleaning and cabin maintenance. Special inspections of aircraft cabin cleaning were carried out in Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad. “Aircraft cleanliness is extremely important. It is important to maintain your brand at the highest standards,” the spokesman quoted PIA Chief Executive Officer Adrian Hamilton-Manns as saying. “Maintaining aircraft in excellent condition is our priority,” the PIA CEO said. “This is the beginning of the process and pace at which aircraft will be maintained in optimal condition,” he said. He pledged to continue initiatives aimed at promoting high standards of cleanliness, quality and service at PIA. Shields and certificates were distributed among employees who played a prominent role in the cleaning process. Cash prizes were also awarded to employees who performed their duties exceptionally well. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: LHC rejects plea for directions to legislation on marital rape
items.description: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) has dismissed a public interest petition seeking directions to the federal and provincial governments to legislate on marital rape, holding that a constitutional court cannot compel the legislature to enact a particular law or create a new offence. Justice Abher Gul Khan clarified that the ruling neither endorses violence or abuse within marriage, nor prevents the Parliament or any provincial assembly from taking up the matter. Areej Sohail Bhutta, a lawyer, filed the petition, stating that she had encountered women clients who complained of non-consensual sexual conduct within their marriages. She argued that the law lacked a distinct statutory framework for sexual violence within marriage. She sought directions for legislative measures, including amendments to sections 375 and 376 of the Pakistan Penal Code. A court can’t force the legislature to enact a law or create an offence, observes the judge Justice Khan observed that the Constitution divides powers among the legislature, the executive and the judiciary, and that judicial review does not authorise courts to assume legislative functions. She said Article 199 empowers the high court to issue directions for the enforcement of fundamental rights. However, she maintained, there is a distinction between directing an authority to perform an existing constitutional or statutory obligation and compelling the legislature to enact a particular law or create a new offence. The judge noted that articles 9, 14 and 25 protect the security, dignity and equality of a person, while articles 25(3) and 34 allow special protections for women and promote their participation in national life. She said Article 35, which requires the state to protect marriage and the family, does not provide a licence for violence against a spouse. Justice Khan observed that foreign laws can provide comparative guidance, but cannot override Pakistan’s Constitution or replace the judgment of its legislature. She said any proposed legal framework also has to be examined in the light of the Constitution, existing laws and the injunctions of Islam. The judge noted that under Article 142(b), the Parliament and provincial assemblies are competent to legislate on criminal law, procedure and evidence. “The question whether an additional offence, a separate statutory provision or a further protective mechanism is required, is essentially a matter of legislative policy,” the judge observed. Citing Supreme Court judgments, including Tika Iqbal Muhammad Khan versus Pervez Musharraf (PLJ 2008 SC 500), the judge observed, “A court cannot issue a mandamus compelling the legislature to enact a particular law.” The judge noted that the petitioner had neither challenged a specific statutory provision as unconstitutional nor identified an authority’s failure to perform an existing legal duty. She said the relief sought would require the court to direct legislation according to a model proposed by the petitioner, amounting to interference in the legislative process. The judge stressed that the decision does not diminish a woman’s dignity or bodily integrity because of marriage, or endorse coercion and abuse within marriage. The judge dismissed the petition to the extent of the relief sought. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: Bavaria’s speaker tipped to become Germany’s first woman president
items.description: GERMAN Chancellor Friedrich Merz (left) shakes hands with Ilse Aigner, the speaker of Bavaria’s state parliament, upon arrival at the Christian Social Union party’s congress in Munich.—AFP BERLIN: Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner is expected to become Germany’s next president in 2027, the first woman to serve as its head of state, conservative ruling party sources said on Friday. Aigner, 61, now the speaker of the southern state’s regional assembly, would replace outgoing President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, a Social Democrat, in the largely ceremonial post. Steinmeier, who took office in 2017, will reach the limit of two five-year terms in March next year. Aigner belongs to the CSU, the Bavarian sister party of the centre-right CDU of Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who is supporting the choice of Aigner, the party sources said. If her nomination is confirmed at a CDU/CSU meeting on Monday, she would be all but certain to be formally elected on Jan 30 by both houses of parliament and civil society representatives. Aigner’s political appeal owes much to a trademark Bavarian warmth, and her appearances in a traditional dirndl dress at beer festivals have made her a familiar figure across the state. Supporters see her consensual approach as an asset in an increasingly polarised country, where the far-right, anti-immigration and pro-Russian AfD party has reached record levels of popularity. In a recent speech, Aigner called for a “reconciled society”, which could provide a guiding theme for a presidential role. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: Lost in translation? Japanese minister blames X for diplomatic embarrassment
items.description: TOKYO: A Japanese minister blamed Elon Musk’s X social media platform on Friday for almost plunging him into diplomatic hot water, after its automatic translation feature implied he did not know the names of world leaders he was meeting. Trade Minister Ryosei Akazawa assured reporters that he knew the identity of the current prime minister of Bangladesh after a post with photos of the two included the name of ousted premier Sheikh Hasina in its translated version. “This is actually a serious matter. It is possible that the Bangladeshi public might be left with the impression that, Japan’s Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry does not even know who our (Bangladeshi) prime minister is,” Akazawa told journalists. His original Japanese-language post on X on Oct 28, accompanied by photos, stated that he met visiting Bangladeshi Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. But the platform’s machine-translation tool incorrectly changed the English version to make Akazawa seem to declare that he met Sheikh Hasina, who has lived in exile in India since an uprising in 2024. Making matters worse, it was not the first time Akazawa had fallen foul of a translation snafu on the platform. He said a similar mistake occurred after he posted about his online meeting with Kuwait’s Oil Minister Tareq Al-Roumi on Thursday -- with the automatic translation feature saying he held talks with Qatar’s energy minister. Akazawa added that his translated post on a meeting with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had also stated an incorrect name. “I experienced this three times,” he said, appealing to X to fix the translation tool. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: JUI-F decries ‘coordinated campaign’ against Fazl
items.description: • Slams alleged drone filming of leaders’ homes, character assassination on social media • Maulana calls for transparency in foreign investment deals QUETTA / LARKANA: The JUI-F staged protests in different parts of Sindh and Balochistan on Friday, decrying what it called a “coordinated character assassination campaign” against its leader, Maulana Fazlur Rehman. In Balochistan, protests were held in district headquarters across the province, including Quetta, Khuz­dar, Awaran, Musakhel, Harnai, Lasbela, Qila Saifullah, Ziarat, Nasirabad, Jaffarabad, Chaman, Pishin, Kalat, Mastung and Kohlu. Party office-bearers, workers, religious scholars, political and social figures participated in the demonstrations, expressing their solidarity with the Maulana. Addressing the gatherings, speakers praised the Maulana’s role in safeguarding the Constitution, democracy, parliamentary supremacy, religious values and public rights. They said the alleged aerial surveillance of his private residence through a drone and the subsequent circulation of the footage on social media were unacceptable in any civilised society. They emphasised that the protection of privacy and the sanctity of one’s home were fundamental rights of every citizen, adding that unjustified interference in anyone’s private life violated moral, legal and constitutional principles. The speakers said it was deeply regrettable that political differences were being turned into personal vendettas, character assassination, unethical campaigns and violations of personal privacy. Such actions, they argued, could intensify political tensions and create unrest and resentment in society. In democratic societies, differences of opinion should be addres­sed through dialogue, arguments and constitutional struggle rather than targeting individuals’ private lives or launching negative propaganda campaigns on social media. They demanded an immediate, transparent and impartial investigation into the alleged drone filming of Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s residence. They called for those responsible, including the individuals allegedly involved behind the scenes, to be identified and dealt with in accordance with the law. They also condemned the use of social media for character assassination, false allegations and organized negative campaigns instead of promoting political debate and public awareness. They stressed that those involved in such activities must be brought to justice. Meanwhile, a meeting of JUI-F Sindh leaders expressed concern over the drone filming of the residence of its general secretary Maulana Rashid Mehmood Soomro, the issuance of NAB and FIA notices to Mufti Asad Mahmood, Kamran Murtaza and other leaders, and the sealing of shops in various cities. Terming them acts of government panic and political vendetta, the gathering insisted that the Maulana and his party were being subjected to vindictive action for raising their voice against the “Form 47 government”, for the unity of the provinces, the NFC Award and the possible 18th Constitutional Amend­ment, and against what they termed conspiracies to seize the provinces’ mineral resources. They stressed, however, that the party would not be intimidated and would continue its constitutional, legal and democratic struggle. The meeting announced that, on the directive of the party chief and in line with a policy of non-violence, protests would be held on highways and major roads. Transparency in investments Meanwhile, addressing a gathering of the Jamiat Talaba Islam in Islamabad, the Maulana called for transparency in agreements with foreign investors, particularly those involving Pakistan’s mineral resources, stressing that the country’s natural wealth should not be exploited through secret arrangements at the expense of its people. He said his party was not oppo­sed to investment from China, the US or multinational companies, but all agreements must be made public, with clearly defined shares of profits for Pakistan, foreign investors and local communities. “We are not against anyone’s inv­estment, but there must be transparency in the process and agreements. The nation should be informed about the conditions under which contracts are signed,” he said. The Maulana also alleged that the government was using security measures in tribal districts to facilitate illegal trade routes. Referring to recurring curfews in parts of the tribal belt, he questioned why restrictions were im­­posed for two days a week while the remaining five days were apparently considered free of terrorism. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: SC calls for scrutiny of illegal power connections
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Friday underlined the need for a microscopic examination of the role of individuals involved in the theft, unauthorised sale and private siphoning of electricity, rather than supplying it through authorised channels. The observation came from a two-judge SC bench, comprising Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar and Justice Irfan Saadat Khan, which was hearing a bail-cancellation petition in a case where a person suffered an electric shock after a power wire snapped. In a six-page order, Justice Mazhar emphasised the need for a thorough examination of current practices by Wapda and the concerned utility companies, observing that it was inconceivable that electricity could be supplied without the knowledge of Wapda, or the concerned utility company and its officials. Petitioner Ali Asghar Khokhar, a resident of Khuhawar Street, Larkana, had filed a criminal petition before the SC seeking cancellation of bail granted to respondent Anwar Ali Kori by the Sindh High Court’s Larkana circuit bench on Oct 20, 2025. Wonders how ‘unauthorised’ supply rackets run under Wapda officials’ noses The case stemmed from an incident in March 2024, when Noor Hussain, the petitioner’s brother, suffered an electric shock after a PVC wire broke and came into contact with a high-tension line. Subsequently, an FIR was registered at Rehmatpur police station in Larkana against Anwar Ali Kori and other Wapda officials. The allegation was that the co-accused, including Wapda officials and the respondent, were supplying electricity to people in their shops by laying a special line from the disposal phase line and running an electric wire over the complainant’s shops. The complainant, who appeared in person before the SC, argued that the high court had granted bail without examining the facts and the incriminating material collected by the investigating officer (IO). However, the SC noted that the high court had granted bail to the respondent predominantly on the grounds of a nine-month delay in lodging the FIR, besides the fact that the role attributed to the respondent was one of negligence. Furthermore, the high court’s order also reflected the IO’s statement that the respondent had no contact with Wapda officials. Therefore, after considering the relevant factors, the high court had reached the tentative assessment that the allegations levelled in the FIR required further inquiry and accordingly confirmed the bail order, the SC observed. It added that the matter at hand also required further inquiry and that, unless a full-dress trial was conducted, the role and guilt of the accused persons implicated in the case could not be established. The SC recalled that, when the complainant was asked how he was powering his shop, he said the respondent was working as a contractor in collusion with Wapda officials and supplying electricity to his shop against monetary consideration. He added that he had never been issued a bill by Wapda or any other utility company. However, after arguing at some length, the complainant himself stated that since the trial was pending, he did not wish to press for cancellation of the respondent’s bail. The SC observed that the high court’s order granting bail did not require any interference and directed the court office to transmit a copy of the order to the Wapda chairman for information. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: Santé mentale : L’UE hausse le ton face à TikTok
items.description: La Commission européenne durcit le ton face à TikTok. Bruxelles demande au réseau social de revoir en profondeur son système de recommandation de contenus, estimant que ses flux personnalisés peuvent favoriser des « spirales » de vidéos susceptibles de nuire au bien-être et à la santé mentale des utilisateurs, notamment des mineurs. Cette nouvelle procédure pourrait coûter cher à la plateforme. En cas d’infraction au règlement européen sur les services numériques (DSA), TikTok pourrait se voir infliger une amende pouvant atteindre 6 % de son chiffre d’affaires annuel mondial. Le principal point de tension concerne le fonctionnement du flux « Pour toi ». L’algorithme analyse les interactions de chaque utilisateur, notamment les vidéos regardées, likées ou partagées, afin de lui proposer des contenus similaires. Selon la Commission européenne, ce mécanisme peut toutefois conduire certains utilisateurs à être exposés de manière répétée à des contenus portant sur des sujets sensibles comme la tristesse, la solitude ou l’image de soi. Le risque est de voir se former des « rabbit holes », ces spirales de contenus dans lesquelles l’utilisateur s’enfonce progressivement, en visionnant toujours davantage de publications similaires. Un phénomène que Bruxelles juge particulièrement préoccupant pour les personnes vulnérables et les mineurs. La Commission reproche également à TikTok de ne pas toujours respecter suffisamment les préférences exprimées par ses utilisateurs. Lorsqu’un internaute indique qu’un type de contenu ne l’intéresse plus, l’algorithme pourrait continuer à lui proposer des vidéos similaires. Bruxelles estime que cette logique peut entrer en contradiction avec les exigences du DSA, qui impose aux grandes plateformes d’évaluer et de réduire les risques liés à leurs services. L’Union européenne demande donc à TikTok d’accorder davantage de contrôle aux utilisateurs sur les contenus qui leur sont recommandés et de mieux prendre en compte leurs choix. La plateforme avait déjà procédé à plusieurs modifications de son système de recommandation. Mais pour la Commission, ces mesures restent insuffisantes et nécessitent des changements plus profonds, susceptibles de toucher directement au fonctionnement d’un modèle économique largement fondé sur la captation de l’attention. La Commission européenne prépare parallèlement un durcissement plus large de son cadre de protection des mineurs sur les réseaux sociaux. La pression ne vient toutefois pas uniquement de l’Europe. Aux États-Unis, TikTok et d’autres grandes plateformes font également face à de nombreuses procédures judiciaires engagées par des familles, des établissements scolaires et plusieurs États, qui les accusent de contribuer à la dégradation de la santé mentale des jeunes. The post Santé mentale : L’UE hausse le ton face à TikTok appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ouagadougou : Un dispositif d'accueil en préparation pour les orpailleurs expulsés de Guinée
items.description: Le retour des orpailleurs burkinabè expulsés de Guinée mobilise les autorités nationales. Face à l'arrivée progressive de ces compatriotes, les acteurs de la réponse humanitaire s'activent pour leur accueil dans des conditions dignes. Présidée par le gouverneur de la région du Kadiogo, Abdoulaye Bassinga, la réunion d'urgence du Conseil régional de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CORESUR) a permis de faire le point de la situation et de planifier les dispositions nécessaires à leur prise en charge. La réunion se tient ce vendredi 6 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Selon les données communiquées au cours de la rencontre, à la date du 5 novembre 2026, un total de 3 533 personnes avait été recensé à Koloko et à Bobo-Dioulasso. Parmi elles figurent 2 428 hommes, 209 femmes et 896 enfants. Ces chiffres pourraient évoluer au fil des arrivées, puisque de nombreux compatriotes se trouvent encore sur le territoire malien, où s'organise une partie de leur retour vers le Burkina Faso. La ville de Bobo-Dioulasso constitue le principal point d'entrée et le premier site d'accueil de ces personnes. C'est à partir de cette localité que sera organisée leur répartition en fonction de leurs régions de provenance ou de destination. Ouagadougou constitue également un deuxième site important dans le dispositif d'accueil. Certains y transiteront avant de rejoindre leurs localités respectives. Une vue des membres du CORESUR Sur le terrain, le dispositif d'acheminement commence progressivement à se mettre en place. Deux cars étaient déjà arrivés à Bobo-Dioulasso au moment de la réunion. Une cinquantaine d'autres véhicules étaient attendus d'ici au petit matin du samedi 7 novembre 2026. Les autorités anticipent ainsi l'arrivée d'environ 4 000 personnes à Bobo-Dioulasso dans les prochaines heures. Pour mieux apprécier l'ampleur des besoins et anticiper les difficultés liées à cette opération, le Conseil national de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CONASUR) a dépêché une vingtaine de personnes sur le terrain. Cette équipe est chargée d'évaluer la situation et de contribuer à l'organisation de la prise en charge des personnes concernées. Au-delà de leur acheminement vers le territoire national, l'enjeu est de leur réserver un accueil digne, en tenant compte de leurs besoins et de leur vulnérabilité, notamment ceux des femmes et des enfants. La coordination entre les différents sites d'accueil et les acteurs mobilisés apparaît donc essentielle pour éviter les difficultés dans la gestion de ces arrivées massives. Pour apporter une prise en charge conséquente, le CORESUR a mis en place des commissions. Il s'agit entre autres de la commission accueil et hébergement. Cette commission est chargée d'accueillir, de vérifier l'identité des personnes et d'assurer leur sécurité. Elle est assurée par les directions régionales du ministère en charge de la solidarité et de la sécurité. Il y a la commission santé. Elle est pilotée par la direction régionale de la santé et la Croix-Rouge. Elle prendra en charge les cas de maladie et la prise en charge psychosociale. La commission eau et assainissement est chargée d'assurer l'approvisionnement en eau potable et la gestion des toilettes et le dispositif de lave-mains. Elle est assurée par le ministère en charge de l'eau et de l'asainissement et les différents arrondissements. Les sites d'accueil seront connus à l'issue de la réunion. Rama Diallo Lefaso.net

items.description: The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) is expected to summon a nurse for further engagement next week following a controversial TikTok livestream allegedly showing a pregnant patient in visible distress. The incident, which has triggered concerns about patient privacy, professional conduct and the dignity of people receiving medical care, came to the attention of the Ministry of Health after a post by a concerned individual on social media. The Ministry’s Public Relations Officer, Tony Goodman, disclosed the Council’s planned action in a Facebook post on Friday, October 6, saying he had been reliably informed that the nurse was expected to be invited for further engagement. “The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) is following up on the matter concerning this nurse. I am reliably informed that she is expected to be invited by the Council next week for further engagement,” he wrote. Livestream sparks outrage A Facebook user, Dickson Assan, who reported the incident to the Ghana Health Service (GHS), said he came across the TikTok Live session in the early hours of the day and was disturbed by what he witnessed. The host, who appeared to be a nurse, was broadcasting a visibly distressed pregnant patient, he posted. He said that during the livestream, the host was seen rubbing the patient’s back, apparently to comfort her. However, the movement attracted inappropriate comments and mockery from some viewers, according to the user. He said the situation became more troubling when a viewer raised concerns about the appropriateness of the broadcast, only to be met with insults from other participants. The Facebook user also alleged that the host had displayed a Mobile Money (MoMo) number on the livestream and solicited contributions from viewers while the patient was in distress. He questioned the conduct of a healthcare worker who, instead of protecting the privacy of a vulnerable patient, appeared to be turning the situation into social media content and an opportunity to solicit money.

items.title: A Preposterous, Overpriced, Beautiful Disaster of a Car
items.description: The most important Cybertruck ever built is probably still parked somewhere on the grounds of Mar-a-Lago. In August 2024, Donald Trump stood on the driveway of his Palm Beach club and circled a custom version of Tesla’s notorious, angular electric truck. Wrapped in a giant photo of his bloodied face after the assassination attempt that summer, the car was a gift from the MAGA influencer Adin Ross during a livestreamed interview. “Wow, that’s an Elon!” Trump said. When Trump returned to the presidency, Elon Musk’s truck became a defining symbol of his second term—a MAGA hat on wheels . Like the president himself, the Cybertruck is thought of differently by different people: brash, unsophisticated, or badass. And like the world’s richest man and former head of DOGE, the Cybertruck moves fast and breaks things with little regard for anything in its way. If nothing else, the Cybertruck is unique: Here is a car that is marketed as bulletproof and has a windshield wiper (only one wiper) that Musk has compared to a “katana.” Now the Cybertruck is about to be something else: discontinued. Early this morning, Musk announced on X that he will wind down production of the Cybertruck by the middle of next year to free up factory space to make Cybercabs, the robotaxis that Tesla is attempting to roll out across the country. No matter how you feel about it, the Cybertruck will go down as a tremendous flop in Silicon Valley history. When the car was first released, in November 2023, Musk called it the “best product” that he’s ever released. As Musk bankrolled Trump’s 2024 presidential run and then joined him in Washington, MAGA supporters enthusiastically embraced the Cybertruck. Fast-forward to 2026, and almost no one wants to buy one. The shift has been telling: The midterms were disastrous for Musk, who blew nearly $500 million boosting unsuccessful Republican candidates, especially in Texas, where Tesla is based. Musk’s discontinuation of the Cybertruck may be seen, among other things, as political triage, a way of wiping his hands clean of a car that liberals have branded as the “Deplorean.” [ Read: My day inside America’s most hated car ] Still, it would be a mistake to remember the truck as nothing more than the apotheosis of two years of Trumpian (and Muskian) excess. The Cybertruck was a meme and a culture-war totem, but it was also just a car. And on that front, Musk’s creation was especially a letdown. When he first announced the car in 2019, it was a revelation, no matter how ugly: After proving that electric cars could be more than just souped-up golf carts, his car company would now bring EVs to the masses. The Cybertruck, Musk promised, would start at just $40,000, a fraction of the cost of Tesla’s other cars at the time. By the time the Cybertruck was actually for sale, it came with a sticker price of $100,000. In some ways, the truck was doomed from the beginning: Building a vehicle that ignores the principles of basic aerodynamics isn’t exactly cheap or easy. Dogged by one problem after the next—stainless-steel panels that can fall off, a faulty accelerator pedal that can get stuck and turn the car into a cruise missile—the Cybertruck did not entice very many people to actually put up the money for one. Within a week of the vehicle’s unveiling, Musk said that 250,000 had preordered one. But in three years, he has sold a total of only 70,000 Cybertrucks. In spite of all the problems, the Cybertruck actually is a pretty fun car. It’s difficult to maneuver and more than a little impractical. But you can’t take a Zoom call from the front seat of a Toyota Camry, or have that vehicle make fart noises when a passenger sits down. Musk’s creation was absurd, but it was different. Few other vehicles can say that. America desperately needs what the Cybertruck could have been. Electric cars offer the possibility of redesigning vehicles from the ground up. In China, you can buy EVs with built-in fridges and headlights that can project movies. In the U.S., however, automakers have mostly just duped the gas cars we’re all familiar with. Even during this moment of high gas prices, Americans have been stubbornly unwilling to go electric. It’s hard not to wonder how many more electric cars would be on the streets if the Cybertruck had actually lived up to its original promise. The Cybertruck was not the best product Musk ever made—not even close—but it’s the product that reveals the most about his motivations and impulses. It is a cautionary tale of Musk’s habit of overpromising and under-delivering. (Data centers in space! Robots that can water your plants !) Most of all, the Cybertruck is another reminder—in this case, a nearly 7,000-pound one—that the influence of the world’s richest man does have limits.

items.title: Kenya : 200 ans de prison pour le gourou du massacre de Shakahola
items.description: La Haute Cour de Mombasa a condamné, vendredi 6 novembre 2026, le prédicateur kényan Paul Mackenzie à 200 ans de prison pour le meurtre de 191 personnes, dont 190 enfants, dans l'affaire du massacre de Shakahola. Le chef religieux était accusé d'avoir poussé ses fidèles à mourir de faim au nom de croyances religieuses. Le verdict est tombé au terme d'une procédure judiciaire particulièrement suivie au Kenya. La juge Diana Kavedza, de la Haute Cour de Mombasa, a prononcé deux peines de 100 ans d’emprisonnement contre Paul Nthenge Mackenzie, fondateur de l'Église Good News International. Ces peines devront être purgées successivement, portant la durée totale de sa condamnation à 200 ans. Selon les conclusions de la justice, le prédicateur a organisé le déplacement de ses fidèles vers la forêt de Shakahola, dans le comté de Kilifi, où il leur aurait ordonné de jeûner jusqu'à la mort afin de rencontrer Jésus. La magistrate lui a attribué la responsabilité pénale principale dans cette tragédie, estimant que les enseignements religieux avaient servi à organiser et à imposer les pratiques meurtrières. Sur les 191 victimes concernées par les chefs d'accusation, 183 sont mortes de faim, tandis que les huit autres ont été victimes d'homicides directs, notamment par suffocation, strangulation ou violences physiques. La majorité des victimes étaient des enfants. La juge a notamment relevé que certains fidèles avaient été empêchés de quitter les lieux et que des gardes veillaient à l'application des consignes de jeûne. Vingt-huit autres personnes ont également été condamnées dans cette affaire. Elles étaient notamment accusées d'avoir participé à l'application des directives du prédicateur, à la surveillance des fidèles ou encore à la dissimulation des corps. Le pasteur adjoint de Mackenzie, Smart Mwakalama, a écopé de 160 ans de prison. L'affaire avait éclaté en avril 2023, après l'intervention des autorités à la suite de signalements faisant état de décès suspects dans la forêt de Shakahola. Les opérations de fouilles et d'exhumation avaient progressivement révélé l'ampleur du drame. Au total, 429 corps ont été retrouvés sur le site, selon les autorités kényanes. Les 191 meurtres jugés dans cette procédure constituent une partie de ce bilan. L'enquête avait également mis en évidence les conditions d'isolement des adeptes, auxquels le prédicateur aurait déconseillé le recours aux soins médicaux et à l'éducation. Les révélations avaient suscité une vive indignation au Kenya et relancé le débat sur l'encadrement des organisations religieuses. Arrêté en avril 2023, Paul Mackenzie reste également concerné par d'autres procédures judiciaires, notamment pour des faits liés au terrorisme, à la maltraitance d'enfants et à la torture. Avec cette condamnation historique, la justice kényane entend sanctionner l'un des épisodes les plus meurtriers de manipulation religieuse de l'histoire récente du pays.

items.title: Un chaton asphyxié à Sidi Bouzid | Plainte déposée
items.description: L'Association Rahma pour la protection des animaux à Sousse a décidé de saisir la justice suite à la découverte d'un nouvel acte de cruauté commis à l'encontre d'un chaton, retrouvé mort dans des conditions particulièrement violentes. Selon les premiers éléments d'information, les faits se sont déroulés à Sidi Bouzid, où un individu a délibérément enfermé l'animal à l'intérieur d'une bouteille en plastique, entraînant sa mort par asphyxie, avant de l'abandonner dans un endroit isolé. A l'appel de l'association, l'avocat Amine Harchani s'est porté volontaire pour assurer la défense et la représentation légale de l'association. Dans une déclaration accordée aux médias, Me Harchani a précisé que la scène avait été documentée par des citoyens, permettant ainsi de constituer un dossier transmis aux autorités judiciaires afin d'établir les responsabilités. Y. N. L’article Un chaton asphyxié à Sidi Bouzid | Plainte déposée est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Tenue à Nouakchott du 21ème congrès maghrébin de radiologie et d’imagerie médicale
items.description: Les travaux du 21e Congrès maghrébin de radiologie et d'imagerie médicale ont débuté ce vendredi à Nouakchott, en présence de médecins, de spécialistes et d'experts venus de Mauritanie, d'Algérie, du Maroc, de Tunisie, du Sénégal, du Mali, de la Côte d'Ivoire et de la France. Organisé par l’Association mauritanienne de radiologie et d’imagerie médicale, ce congrès se déroule sur trois jours et a pour objectif de favoriser l’échange d’expériences et de savoir-faire entre les spécialistes, et de débattre des avancées scientifiques et techniques dans le domaine de la radiologie et de l’imagerie médicale. Le président de l’association, le Pr Mohamed Beddi, a déclaré que l’accueil de ce congrès par la Mauritanie s’inscrit dans la continuité de ses traditions arabes et africaines en matière d’organisation de rencontres scientifiques, soulignant que cet événement rassemble des spécialistes du Maghreb, d’Afrique de l’Ouest et de France, ce qui permet l’échange d’expériences et de connaissances ainsi que le renforcement de la coopération professionnelle. Ould Beddi a ajouté que la radiologie et l’imagerie médicale constituent un pilier essentiel du diagnostic et contribuent à la prise en charge thérapeutique des patients, ce qui nécessite une formation continue et un suivi constant des avancées techniques. Il a précisé que les thèmes du congrès avaient été choisis pour répondre aux exigences de l’évolution dans le domaine de la radiologie, notamment en ce qui concerne l’intelligence artificielle et l’imagerie médicale interventionnelle, se disant convaincu que le programme scientifique répondra aux attentes des participants, compte tenu de la compétence des intervenants et de l’importance des thèmes abordés. Le président de l'association a remercié les plus hautes autorités du pays pour leur soutien et pour avoir mis à disposition les moyens nécessaires à la réussite du congrès avant de saluer la contribution des partenaires des secteurs public et privé à son organisation. Le programme scientifique du congrès comprend des thèmes liés à l’imagerie des maladies gynécologiques, du système digestif et des urgences, ainsi qu’à l’intelligence artificielle et à la radiologie interventionnelle, à travers des conférences et des présentations spécialisées abordant les dernières technologies et pratiques dans ces domaines.

items.title: Meghan’s father Thomas Markle appears in court over child sex abuse material
items.description: Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has appeared in court after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material. Markle was arrested on a federal complaint alleging he held images that show child sex abuse, the US Department of Justice (DoJ) said. The 82-year-old was arrested in Florida after the FBI searched two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented for almost 20 years. He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, the US Department of Justice (DoJ) said. Markle has previously denied allegations of possessing images of child sex abuse, calling them “sick lies”. Markle’s court hearing lasted for 30 minutes, and the charges were laid out against him by federal prosecutor Courtenay Derry, according to the BBC’s US partner CBS News. He was brought into court in a wheelchair, escorted by two US Marshals. Markle was wearing black trousers and a black T-shirt. The court ordered Markle to submit to home detention at his assisted living facility in Florida and electronic monitoring. No plea was taken during the hearing, and an arraignment date in California will be determined in due course, a joint statement from the DoJ and the US Attorney’s Office Central California said. The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have not commented on Markle’s arrest. FBI director Kash Patel said authorities “moved quickly” when arresting Markle. “Mr Markle allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions,” Patel said. He added that the FBI would “use every single resource at our disposal to protect innocent kids – any predator who targets children will have zero safe haven in this country or anywhere they try to hide”. Markle was arrested after the FBI, acting on warrants, searched storage units in LA registered to him which he had rented since 2008, with the last payment being made in October this year. Inside the units the FBI says agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material. Thomas Markle appeared in court on Friday Witnesses “positively identified” Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material. In those images, the man pictured “appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s”, which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades as Markle is currently 82 years old. Last month, police in the Philippines obtained a warrant to examine devices allegedly removed from Markle’s former home in the country. Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes, were handed to officers by Meghan’s half brother Thomas Markle Jr. Markle Sr moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May. He was then reportedly living in a Florida rehabilitation centre learning to walk again after having his leg amputated. In October, London’s Metropolitan Police confirmed that it had received a letter in 2019 making a “number of claims” relating to Markle Sr. The Met said information contained in the letter, which related to allegations against Meghan’s father outside the UK, was passed on to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, but it did not share it with other law enforcement agencies. The force has since voluntarily referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IPOC) over its handling of the letter. In a statement released in October after the allegations against Markle Sr emerged, the Duchess of Sussex said: “I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed.” Meghan has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year.
