items.title: Déploiement de l’armée algérienne au Niger : Abdelaziz Rahabi recadre sèchement l’UE
items.description: L’Union européenne a réagi à la décision de l’Algérie de répondre favorablement à la demande du Niger de déployer des unités de l’Armée nationale populaire sur son territoire. Anouar El Anouni, porte-parole de l’UE, a indiqué que Bruxelles cherchait à obtenir de « plus « éclaircissements sur la portée, l’objectif ainsi que la base de ce déploiement ». Une sortie qui a fait réagir Abdelaziz Rahabi. L’ancien ministre et ex-ambassadeur d’Algérie à Madrid a recadré sèchement l’UE en lui demandant de « quel droit », elle demande des éclaircissements. Abdelaziz Rahabi : « Déploiement d’unités de l’ANP au Niger : l’UE demande des éclaircissements. De quel droit ? » « Un des porte-paroles du l’Union européenne vient de déclarer que les Européens suivaient de près le déploiement d’unités algériennes au Niger et que l’UE attendait des « éclaircissements sur la portée, l'objectif et la base de ce déploiement … » A la lecture de cette déclaration, il est difficile de ne pas être surpris de voir l’UE réagir de la sorte à une mise en œuvre d’un accord militaire annoncé entre deux pays voisins et dont les conditions ne concernent que les deux Etats », a dénoncé Abdelaziz Rahabi. Le diplomate algérien juge encore « plus grave » que le même porte-parole et « sans la moindre réserve pourtant d’usage sur les questions extraeuropéennes, déclare expressément attendre des éclaircissements de l’Algérie. » Rahabi dénonce l’attitude de l’UE envers l’Algérie Abdelaziz Rahabi critique ensuite l’attitude de l’Union européenne vers l’Algérie. « Ainsi, l’Europe s’adresse à nous comme si nous étions tenus par un engagement conventionnel avec elle sur ces questions, ou comme si elle représentait une organisation militaire en charge du Sahel. A défaut d’avoir ce statut, elle nous suggère de la consulter au préalable sur cette région ou pour le moins lui devoir des éclaircissements à posteriori », dénonce-t-il. Rahabi reproche à l’UE son impuissance de « se départir de ses lectures passéistes » de l’Afrique. Il estime que l’Europe « ne doit pas pouvoir se permettre de douter de la sincérité de ses partenaires et de la souveraineté de leurs mécanismes internes de validation des accords internationaux faute de quoi cela pourrait l’exposer à de réelles demandes d’explications d’Alger. » L’article Déploiement de l’armée algérienne au Niger : Abdelaziz Rahabi recadre sèchement l'UE est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Trump Doubles Down With Miller
items.description: Introspection has never been one of Donald Trump’s more notable attributes. He never accepts blame or course-corrects; he only becomes a more distilled version of himself. And so, faced with rejection at the ballot box on an overwhelming scale, the president responded by replacing his chief of staff, Susie Wiles, with Stephen Miller. Technically speaking, Miller had been Wiles’s second in command, as deputy chief of staff. In reality, Miller was already the administration’s most powerful figure, arguably including Trump himself. Steve Bannon, a former Trump adviser and a Miller ally who was briefly cast as the power behind the throne during Trump’s first term, described Miller earlier this year as Trump’s “prime minister.” In a parliamentary system, the president or monarch is merely the symbolic head of state, whereas the prime minister is the head of government. Wiles, though reputed for her professionalism and competence, held her job for nearly two years by facilitating Trump’s impulses without questioning them. Miller, however, has driven and shaped those impulses. He is fanatically post-liberal. Miller has repeatedly described the opposition as illegitimate. “The Democrat Party is not a political party,” he said last year. “It is a domestic extremist organization.” He has obsessively, and effectively, employed executive actions to circumvent Congress as a lawmaking body. Trump had little use for the legislature even when his allies controlled it. If Miller remains true to form, he will extend his reliance on executive action, and commit the administration to total defiance of any oversight. He is especially driven by his belief that immigration is a plot directed by left-wing elites to destroy traditional America. Miller, more than any other single factor, explains Trump’s baffling choice to blow up his 2024 coalition, which registered shocking gains among Latinos. He has directed the administration’s frantic campaign of mass deportation, acting in the belief that the GOP has four years to permanently reshape American demography or face permanent extinction. Miller, more than any other person, is responsible for unleashing violent havoc on American streets, as masked agents in unmarked vehicles have swept up suspects. He has also virtually shut down legal immigration—except for white South Africans, whom the administration has ostentatiously welcomed. Even Trump, according to The Wall Street Journal , has sometimes complained that Miller’s immigration enforcement has gone too far. Miller’s enforcement regimen is obviously not the sole cause of Trump’s unpopularity. Trump’s tariffs, corruption, cuts to health care, obsession with erecting monuments to or renaming them for himself, and the war with Iran all contributed to the disintegration of his coalition. When J. D. Vance laid all of the blame on the war, absolving every other failure, it sent a signal that the administration would tolerate criticism only in this one, single realm. The signal sent by Miller’s elevation takes that message to the next step. Miller pitched himself to Trump as an advocate of winding down the war with Iran, The New York Times ’ Maggie Haberman reported . His elevation thus combines retreat on a single front—a front many Trump devotees regard as a betrayal of his “America First” principles—with a determination to advance on every other. Trump dwells in a zero-sum world, divided between winners and losers. His instinct in a moment of defeat is to empower an aide who he himself recognizes has at times gone too far. But Trump cannot admit he has failed, or bring himself to show any weakness. Better to go too far than not far enough.

items.title: Sheikh Ibrahim Barsha accepts appointment as interim National Imam of ASWAJ, calls for unity
items.description: A founding member of Ahlussunna Wal Jama’a (ASWAJ) and one of Ghana’s most respected Islamic scholars, Sheikh Ibrahim Barsha, has accepted appointment as the organization’s Interim National Imam. The acceptance came on Friday, November 6, 2026, following Jumu’ah prayers at Masjid Al Bayan in Tamale, where Sheikh Barsha has long served as leader. His appointment by the National Da’awa Council (NADAC) follows the removal of Sheikh Umar Ibrahim Imam from office earlier this week. A Lifetime of Service Sheikh Ibrahim Barsha—also known as Ibrahim Basha Iddris, Mallam Basha, or Sheikh Bayaan—is no stranger to pioneering work. In 1969, he founded the Nuriyya Islamic Institute in Tamale, an institution that would become instrumental in reshaping Islamic education in Ghana. He is widely credited as the initiator of the transformation of traditional madrasas into Anglo-Arabic schools—a reform that bridged classical Islamic learning with modern educational systems. His vision extended beyond the classroom. Sheikh Barsha is considered the pioneer behind the creation of the Ghana Islamic Education Unit, a body that has shaped how Islamic education is delivered and regulated across the country. As a campaigner and architect of the Sunni Islamic movement in Ghana, his credentials for the interim role are unmatched. “An Amanah Before Allah” In a speech delivered after prayers, Sheikh Barsha framed his new role in deeply spiritual terms. “Alhamdulillah, all praise and gratitude belong to Almighty Allah, who guides our affairs and grants us the strength to serve His religion and community,” he began. “I accept this responsibility with humility, a deep sense of duty and a full appreciation of the demands of this office. I recognise that leadership is an Amanah (trust) before Almighty Allah and a responsibility to the people.” A Four-Pillar Roadmap The Interim Imam outlined a clear roadmap for his tenure, built around four priorities: Continuity — Ensuring the smooth running of the Association’s administration and ongoing activities. Reconciliation — Engaging national and regional officers, scholars, and stakeholders to promote consultation and unity. Institutional Strengthening — Bolstering records and administrative structures while ensuring strict adherence to the ASWAJ Constitution. Constitutional Succession — Working with NADAC to facilitate the selection or election of a substantive National Imam. “We will approach each of these priorities with fairness, inclusiveness and a firm commitment to the collective interest of the Association,” he assured. A Call for Calm Addressing the wider ASWAJ community, Sheikh Barsha urged restraint and maturity during the transitional period. “This transitional period calls for patience, maturity, mutual respect and strict adherence to the ASWAJ Constitution,” he said. “I encourage all members to remain calm, avoid divisive comments and actions, and work together in the collective interest of the Association.” He also emphasized that the burden of leadership is shared. “This responsibility is not mine alone; it is a collective trust that requires the support, cooperation and commitment of every member.” Prayers for Healing and Stability Concluding his address, Sheikh Barsha offered prayers for the organization and its members. “May Almighty Allah guide our decisions, heal any divisions, strengthen the bonds of brotherhood and grant us the wisdom to move forward in peace and unity. May He make this transitional period a means of renewed commitment, reconciliation, progress and lasting stability for Ahlussunna Wal Jama’a.” What’s Next for ASWAJ? With Sheikh Barsha now at the helm, attention turns to the organization’s next steps. The Interim Imam’s mandate is transitional, and his stated priority is to guide ASWAJ through a constitutional process towards electing a substantive National Imam. For now, the focus is on stability and unity—themes that have defined Sheikh Barsha’s decades of service to the Muslim community in Ghana and beyond. About Sheikh Ibrahim Barsha Sheikh Ibrahim Barsha is a Ghanaian Islamic preacher, scholar, and founding member of ASWAJ. He founded the Nuriyya Islamic Institute in Tamale in 1969 and serves as leader of Masjidul Bayaan. He is widely credited with pioneering the transformation of traditional madrasas into Anglo-Arabic schools and the creation of the Ghana Islamic Education Unit. He is a leading figure in the Sunni Islamic movement in Ghana.

items.title: Rights on the Ballot Alongside US Congressional Elections
items.description: Click to expand Image A voter picks up an "I Voted" sticker after casting their ballot in the US midterm elections on November 3, 2026. © 2026 AP Photo/George Walker IV Alongside the high-profile congressional and gubernatorial races decided during the United States midterm elections on November 3, human rights were at issue in several state and local ballot measures across the country. In Virginia, voters adopted a measure to automatically restore voting rights to people with felony convictions upon release from prison, ending a lifetime ban that had been in place since the Jim Crow era. Arizona voters rejected and Wisconsin voters approved measures to end diversity, equity, and inclusion practices in education, employment, contracts, and administration, mirroring Trump administration initiatives to dismantle programs to address ongoing impacts of historical discrimination based on race and ethnicity. Vermont voters approved an amendment providing equal protection to individuals regardless of their race, ethnicity, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or national origin. Meanwhile, Missouri voters rejected an effort to restrict the right to abortion care and measures to safeguard abortion rights were successful in Nevada and Virginia but failed in Idaho. Ballot measures on transgender rights also showed mixed results. In Colorado, voters adopted a measure to ban gender-affirming surgeries for youth under 18. In Missouri, one of 27 US states to have a ban on gender-affirming care for youth, voters opted to keep the ban out of the state’s constitution. Virginia voters approved an amendment formally lifting the state’s obsolete ban on same-sex marriage and affirming that two adults may marry regardless of sex, gender, and race. Immigration-related measures were also on several ballots. Colorado voters rejected a measure that would have required state and local law enforcement to coordinate with federal immigration authorities in some circumstances. Voters in Honolulu, Hawaii were consulted on a measure requiring their police department to ensure the constitutional rights of all persons regardless of immigration or citizenship status, and work with federal agents only when required by statute or a court order, though the results are still to be decided. And voters in Chicago, Illinois, said they agreed that the city should seek financial compensation from the federal government for harm caused by immigration enforcement operations. The US Congressional elections may be the biggest story of the week, but voters took up some important human rights issues directly in these initiatives and the impacts will be felt for years to come.

items.description: Quatre corps sans vie ont été découverts ce vendredi sur la rive de Tébène 2, un village situé dans la commune de Thiéppe, dans le département de Kébémer. Selon notre source, une pirogue transportant des candidats à l’émigration clandestine aurait échoué au large de cette localité. La même source indique que plusieurs rescapés auraient pris la fuite après le drame. Toutefois, le nombre exact de candidats à l’émigration clandestine reste inconnu. Interrogé sur cette situation, le maire de Thiéppe, Mouhamed Dia, déplore un phénomène qui, selon lui, est en train de décimer la jeunesse. « Nous déplorons les conditions dans lesquelles les jeunes veulent, coûte que coûte, rejoindre l’Europe », fait remarquer l’édile. Selon lui, il est nécessaire de renforcer les moyens de la brigade territoriale de gendarmerie de Kébémer afin de mieux lutter contre ce phénomène, qui prend de plus en plus d’ampleur dans la zone. items.title: Stephen Miller, l’idéologue extrême de la recolonisation, prend la Maison-Blanche
items.description: Vendredi 6 novembre, Donald Trump a annoncé sur Truth Social que Stephen Miller, défini « l’un de mes conseillers les plus fidèles », remplacerait Susie Wiles au poste de chef de cabinet à partir de lundi. Wiles « rejoindra l’équipe politique de Trump ». Ce remaniement intervient trois jours après la défaite des républicains aux élections de mi-mandat. Plutôt que d'infléchir sa ligne politique, il confie son cabinet dans un moment de chaos de plus en plus visible à son idéologue le plus radical, qui lui voue une loyauté sans limites. Nommé chef adjoint du cabinet pour les politiques et conseiller à la sécurité intérieure en janvier 2025, Miller cumulera désormais le contrôle de l’agenda présidentiel, de l’appareil exécutif et de la sécurité intérieure. Il prend ses fonctions au moment où trois échéances importantes s'alignent : une fuite en avant diplomatique sur l’Ukraine dans l’horizon du G20 américain, une difficile recomposition du parti républicain après sa déroute et l’arrivée en janvier d’une majorité démocrate qui promet d’ouvrir des enquêtes contre l’administration et le clan Trump. Le départ de Susie Wiles pourrait être une rupture d’équilibre pour la Maison-Blanche. Première femme à occuper ce poste, Wiles était la figure d’autorité de l’entourage présidentiel. En janvier 2025, elle avait promis de « tenir les fauteurs de troubles à l’écart de l’aile ouest » Susie Wiles vows to block West Wing troublemakers », Axios , 6 janvier 2025.'> 1 . Venue de la politique électorale floridienne, où elle a dirigé les campagnes de Rick Scott puis de Ron DeSantis, elle incarnait davantage un professionnalisme d’appareil qu’une doctrine. Alors qu’une partie du mouvement MAGA réclamait sa tête, le 18 octobre encore, Trump assurait qu’il n'y avait « zéro chance » qu’il la remplace “Zero chance” that Trump will replace chief of staff Susie Wiles, he says », The Washington Times , 18 octobre 2026.'> 2 . Dans son premier entretien après la défaite, Steve Bannon, particulièrement peu présent à la Maison-Blanche sous le règne de Wiles, avait demandé sa tête. Steve Bannon calls for White House chief of staff Susie Wiles to go after the midterm rout. “Because of the results, they should be removed, and removed immediately.” His first interview since the defeat : https://t.co/c3BExQNz2h pic.twitter.com/9rpO4XIEwE — Steven Edginton (@StevenEdginton) November 6, 2026 Contrairement à Wiles, Miller est un idéologue. Né à Santa Monica en 1985 dans une famille juive ashkénaze, il milite dès le lycée contre les associations étudiantes d’origine mexicaine. Repéré par le polémiste David Horowitz, qui restera son mentor, il coorganise, en mars 2007, un débat sur l’immigration avec Richard Spencer, futur chef de file du suprémacisme blanc américain. En 2009, il devient attaché de presse du sénateur Jeff Sessions, dont il dirigera la communication, et avec qui il coécrit en 2015 un Manuel de l’immigration pour la nouvelle majorité républicaine Immigration Handbook for the New Republican Majority , janvier 2015.'> 3 . Sa vision politique transparaît sans filtre dans plus de 900 courriels adressés aux éditeurs de Breitbart entre mars 2015 et juin 2016, et transmis en 2019 au Southern Poverty Law Center par une ancienne rédactrice du site Stephen Miller’s Affinity for White Nationalism Revealed in Leaked Emails », Hatewatch , Southern Poverty Law Center, 12 novembre 2019.'> 4 . Il y recommande notamment de traiter du roman Le Camp des saints de Jean Raspail . Il propose également de reprendre des contenus d'American Renaissance, un site suprémaciste blanc, et dit admirer la loi sur l'immigration de 1924, qui instaurait des quotas par origine nationale. Selon le SPLC, il y relaie la théorie du grand remplacement. Il a pu transformer sa vision en politique publique lors du premier mandat, en assumant un rôle plus central dans la politique interne lors du retour de Donald Trump à la Maison-Blanche. Conseiller principal du président durant tout le premier mandat, Miller a conçu le décret d'interdiction d'entrée visant plusieurs pays à majorité musulmane, signé le 27 janvier 2017. Il a également défendu la politique de « tolérance zéro », la séparation des familles à la frontière au printemps 2018, ainsi que la fin du programme DACA, qui protégeait les jeunes sans papiers arrivés aux États-Unis alors qu'ils étaient enfants. Cette décision a finalement été bloquée par la Cour suprême en juin 2020 5 . De retour à la Maison-Blanche en janvier 2025 en tant que chef adjoint du cabinet pour les politiques et conseiller à la sécurité intérieure, il dirige de facto la politique migratoire. La presse américaine le décrit comme le véritable dirigeant, surpassant la secrétaire à la Sécurité intérieure, Kristi Noem, qui a quitté l’administration en mars 2026 Stephen Miller, Not Kristi Noem, May Be Driving U.S. Immigration Policy », Forbes , 1er février 2026.'> 6 . Il est également présenté comme l’architecte du déploiement de la Garde nationale dans les villes démocrates et de l’intensification des opérations de l’ICE, ayant fait au moins quatorze blessés par balle entre septembre 2025 et février 2026, dont plusieurs sont morts, y compris deux citoyens américains tués à Minneapolis en janvier 2026 Stephen Miller emerges as key architect of Trump’s offensive on Democratic cities »,CNN, 11 octobre 2025.'> 7 . À l'instar de plusieurs autres figures de la deuxième Maison-Blanche de Donald Trump, Stephen Miller a joué un rôle clef dans la contestation de la défaite de 2020. Le 14 décembre 2020, jour du vote des collèges électoraux, il déclarait sur Fox & Friends : « À l'heure où nous parlons, une liste alternative de grands électeurs dans les États contestés va voter, et nous allons transmettre ces résultats au Congrès. » Stephen Miller, intervention sur Fox & Friends , Fox News , 14 décembre 2020.'> 8 Il citait nommément la Géorgie, le Wisconsin et la Pennsylvanie, trois États remportés par Biden, et affirmait que Trump pouvait encore être certifié vainqueur. Il est d’ailleurs le principal rédacteur des discours de Trump du 6 janvier, jour de l’assaut du Capitole, y compris de celui prononcé ce jour-là devant la Maison-Blanche. Miller a été entendu le 14 avril 2022 par la commission d’enquête de la Chambre des représentants, qui l’a interrogé sur sa contribution à l'écriture de ce texte et sur la question de savoir si le président cherchait à inciter la foule en prononçant notamment la phrase « Fight like hell ». Il a de nouveau témoigné devant un grand jury fédéral en avril 2023, mais n'a jamais été inculpé. Miller, radicalisé très tôt sur la question migratoire, prône une interprétation de l’histoire occidentale à partir d’une thèse extrême : la décolonisation aurait été une erreur et l’Occident devrait donc se lancer dans un processus de recolonisation . Dans un texte publié le 5 janvier, alors que l’opération militaire américaine au Venezuela était en cours, il décrit l’après-1945 comme une « colonisation inversée ». Selon lui, l’Occident aurait démantelé ses empires, financé ses anciennes colonies et ouvert ses frontières, accordant aux arrivants « un traitement juridique et financier préférentiel par rapport aux citoyens autochtones ». Pour lui, « l’expérience néolibérale a été, au fond, une longue forme d’auto-punition des lieux et des peuples qui ont bâti le monde moderne ». Not long after World War II the West dissolved its empires and colonies and began sending colossal sums of taxpayer-funded aid to these former territories (despite have already made them far wealthier and more successful). The West opened its borders, a kind of reverse… — Stephen Miller (@StephenM) January 5, 2026 La Stratégie nationale de sécurité reprend cette analyse en décrivant une Europe menacée d'« effacement civilisationnel ». Trump commente : « Si cette tendance se poursuit, beaucoup de ces pays ne seront plus vivables. » Il est très probable que l’arrivée de Miller au poste de chef de cabinet sera suivie d'une radicalisation de la trajectoire de la Maison-Blanche et de l'ouverture de plusieurs nouveaux fronts, tant internes que géopolitiques. L’article Stephen Miller, l’idéologue extrême de la recolonisation, prend la Maison-Blanche est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le BN-GPB remet 200 tracteurs au ministère de l’Agriculture
items.description: Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de l'Initiative Présidentielle pour la Production Agricole et l’Autosuffisance Alimentaire (IP-P3A), le Bureau National des Grands Projets du Burkina (BN-GPB) a remis les clés de 200 tracteurs au ministre d'État, chargé de l'Agriculture, le Commandant Ismaël Sombié, ce 6 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Ces tracteurs, dotés de 40 chevaux, sont composés de charrues et de herses. Ils ont été remis au ministère de l'Agriculture afin d'accélérer la mécanisation agricole. L'objectif des autorités est d'accroître la production agricole en vue de l'atteinte de l'autosuffisance alimentaire au Burkina Faso. Ces tracteurs sont destinés prioritairement au labour des superficies des coopératives des 8 000 VDP agricoles formés dans le cadre de l'Initiative Présidentielle pour la Production Agricole et l’Autosuffisance Alimentaire (IP-P3A). Ils seront également mis à la disposition des autres producteurs des différentes communes du Burkina Faso. Le ministre de l’Agriculture, le commandant Ismaël Sombié a rappelé la nécessité de la mécanisation du secteur agricole face aux défis climatiques. Pour lui, les producteurs doivent être suffisamment équipés afin de respecter le calendrier agricole. Sans un nombre important de tracteurs, dit-il, les agriculteurs seront confrontés aux conséquences de la pluviométrie. C'est dans cette perspective qu'il a souligné que, depuis quatre ans, le président du Faso s'est fixé pour objectif la mécanisation du secteur agricole à travers l'octroi de machines modernes pour la préparation des sols jusqu'aux récoltes. Une partie des tracteurs©️Faso7 « Aujourd'hui, nous sommes soulagés et nous sommes heureux, en tant que département en charge de l’Agriculture, de recevoir ce lot de tracteurs », a-t-il indiqué. Par ailleurs, l'accent sera mis sur le labour des superficies des VDP agricoles conformément à la vision du Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Selon le commandant Sombié, le président du Faso a voulu, à travers ces VDP, créer un nouveau monde rural formé et équipé pour l'atteinte de l'autosuffisance alimentaire. De plus, il a informé que les superficies qui ont été mises à la disposition des VDP agricoles ont déjà fait l’objet de traitement. Les tracteurs serviront à lancer les activités agricoles. Le présent don va porter à 700 le nombre de tracteurs du parc du ministère. Notons également que les actions combinées de l’IP-P3A et de l'Offensive agropastorale, hydraulique et halieutique ont permis au Burkina Faso d'atteindre, en 2025, un taux de couverture inédit des besoins céréaliers de 124,6 %. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Le BN-GPB remet 200 tracteurs au ministère de l'Agriculture est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Trump promotes Stephen Miller to chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles
items.description: US President Donald Trump replaced chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller on Friday, elevating the architect of some of his toughest domestic policies to run the White House after Republicans lost control of Congress in this week’s midterm elections . The shake-up puts a longtime Trump loyalist and firebrand policy adviser in charge of steering Trump’s agenda as the president prepares to confront a Democratic-led House of Representatives and Senate, and an expected wave of congressional investigations. White House officials told Reuters that Miller’s selection suggests Trump will take an aggressive approach to domestic policy and politics. Miller is a veteran of Trump’s first term in office in 2017-2021. Since Trump’s return to the White House in 2025, Miller has officially been deputy chief of staff under Wiles, but he wielded outsize influence across much of Trump’s domestic agenda and has had the ear of the president. He is perhaps best known for driving Trump’s aggressive immigration crackdown, setting a target of 3,000 arrests a day. In pursuit of that target, federal immigration agents expanded their list of targets to include migrants who had been living in the US for decades. In a social media post, Trump called Miller “one of my most trusted advisers,” and he praised Wiles for doing “an outstanding job”. Trump said the change would take effect on Monday. Wiles, who submitted her resignation on Thursday night, will move to Trump’s political operation, according to a White House official. Wiles, 69, who announced recently that she had been given the all-clear from breast cancer, said in a statement on X that Friday would be her last day in her job. “Serving President Trump in the White House has been the honor of a lifetime,” she wrote. “I’m so proud to have been a part of what we’ve accomplished together from securing our border and cutting taxes to strengthening our economy and putting America First.” Trump had been displeased with his political and communications operations in the run-up to Tuesday’s election as his public approval ratings fell near record lows. This week, he said the White House needed to be “more aggressive” as Democrats retake congressional power, according to a person briefed on the matter. Wiles’ allies in the White House began sharing concerns with others on Wednesday about her potential replacement, the person said. “He’s rewarding those most loyal to him. He’s not changing course,” said another White House official.

items.title: Newsfile to discuss Traffitech-GH fines, drug busts and Parliament’s continued absence of Asante Akyem North MP
items.description: This Saturday’s edition of Newsfile on JoyNews will examine three major issues dominating Ghana’s public discourse, as host Samson Lardy Anyenini leads discussions on road safety enforcement, the fight against drug trafficking and developments in Parliament. The programme, scheduled for Saturday, November 7, 2026, from 8:00 a.m. to 12 noon, will scrutinise the implementation of the Traffitech-GH system, renewed drug seizures and the continued absence of the Member of Parliament for Asante Akyem North from parliamentary proceedings. The first major issue will focus on TraffiTech-GH and whether the new automated traffic enforcement system will deliver safer roads or impose unfair financial burdens on motorists. The system, which became operational on November 1, 2026, is intended to strengthen compliance with road traffic regulations through technology-driven monitoring and enforcement. However, its introduction has attracted criticism from commercial transport operators, who accuse the government of prioritising fines while failing to address the occupation of designated bus stops and pedestrian walkways by traders. The National Road Safety Authority (NRSA) has also raised concerns about faulty traffic lights, missing road signs and faded road markings, warning that these deficiencies could undermine the effectiveness of the system. With the Ghana Police Service urging motorists to verify traffic violation notices before making payments, the programme will examine whether the system is adequately designed to improve road safety while ensuring fairness and transparency in its enforcement. The discussion will also turn to the growing number of drug seizures linked to Ghana and questions about the effectiveness of the country’s border security systems. Recent developments have renewed concerns about Ghana’s role in international drug trafficking networks, particularly following the seizure of 46.7 kilogrammes of cocaine at the Rafic Hariri International Airport in Beirut, Lebanon, in a consignment that originated from Accra. The Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) has defended its decision to allow a suspected trafficker to travel to Lebanon, explaining that it was part of a controlled-delivery operation intended to identify and arrest other members of the international trafficking network. Three foreign nationals have subsequently been arrested in Ghana in connection with the shipment. The concerns have been compounded by a fresh interception of approximately 4.8 tonnes of suspected marijuana by the Ghana Navy at the Volta Lake estuary near Ada, with the consignment allegedly destined for Nigeria. The Minority in Parliament has meanwhile demanded accountability from President John Mahama over what it describes as failures in the country’s border protection arrangements. It has also renewed calls for a parliamentary inquiry into the major drug seizures, raising questions about port security, intelligence coordination and possible institutional weaknesses. Newsfile will interrogate whether the successive seizures reflect failures in Ghana’s border controls or form part of coordinated operations to dismantle international drug trafficking networks. Another significant issue will be Parliament’s resumption for the third meeting of the Second Session of the Ninth Parliament without the Member of Parliament for Asante Akyem North, Ohene Kwame Frimpong. The MP remains in custody in the Netherlands following his arrest at Amsterdam’s Schiphol Airport in May 2026, in connection with a United States extradition request over allegations involving romance scams and money laundering. Two applications for bail have reportedly been unsuccessful, with his extradition hearing scheduled for November 18, 2026. His prolonged absence has raised questions about the constitutional provisions governing an MP’s failure to attend parliamentary sittings and whether his continued detention could put his parliamentary seat at risk. Private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu has cited a 2008 Court of Appeal ruling involving former Nkoranza North MP Eric Amoateng, arguing that the precedent could have implications for Mr Frimpong’s situation, particularly regarding the constitutional requirement for written permission from the Speaker for prolonged absence. The Majority, however, maintains that the seat should not be declared vacant while the MP remains presumed innocent and has not been convicted of any offence. The programme will examine the legal and constitutional implications of his continued absence and what it means for parliamentary representation in Asante Akyem North. With these issues commanding national attention, Saturday’s Newsfile promises a robust examination of road safety, institutional accountability, national security and constitutional governance. Join Samson Lardy Anyenini and his panellists this Saturday, November 7, from 8:00 a.m. to 12 noon on JoyNews and JoyFM 99.7.

items.title: Before buying AI, businesses need to ask better questions
items.description: A recent analysis encouraged Ghanaian entrepreneurs to connect artificial intelligence with practical needs, including customer communication and record-keeping. That is a useful starting point, but it leaves another question: how should a business choose the company providing the technology? A convincing demonstration should begin a discussion, not end it. Before committing money or uploading customer information, owners need to understand what a service delivers, what remains their responsibility, and how they can leave if it disappoints. Request a Demonstration of Your Actual Work Consider a hypothetical printing business in Kumasi comparing two services for preparing quotations. Instead of accepting a supplier’s polished examples, the owner could provide a fictional order and an approved price list. Ask each provider to complete the same task. Include an unavailable paper size, an unclear delivery instruction and a request for an unauthorised discount. Observe whether the system asks questions or invents answers. Keep the expected result beside the output. Check calculations independently rather than accepting a fluent explanation as evidence. Also ask whether a spreadsheet or standard template would solve the problem. The purpose is to improve a business process, not buy an AI feature merely because it is fashionable. Let an employee who missed the sales presentation repeat the exercise using only the supplied instructions. If routine work still depends on the vendor’s representative, include the additional training and support required in your evaluation and budget before giving the wider team access. Establish What Happens to Your Information Before uploading real records, ask where information is processed, how long it is retained and whether it is used to train models. Request answers covering the particular subscription under consideration. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre recommends assessing external AI providers and controlling data sent outside an organisation. Its guidance also emphasises limiting access to necessary functions. For the printing business, an early trial needs neither customer addresses nor unpublished designs. Use fictional examples until appropriate arrangements have been checked. Ask who can access account history, how departing employees lose access and how deletion requests are handled. Keep the supplier’s written commitments alongside your own operating instructions. Make Clear Communication an Acceptance Test A useful service should help employees explain the business accurately, not simply produce more words. Teams hoping to humanize AI drafts should preserve prices, deadlines and conditions while improving readability. Compare a revised quotation with the source document. Has a possible delivery date become a guarantee? Has the deposit requirement disappeared? OWASP identifies convincing but inaccurate information as a risk in language model applications and recommends verification against trusted sources. Test messages with the staff who answer customer questions. Where communication involves Twi or another Ghanaian language, include competent speakers rather than judging only the English version. Ask the supplier how corrections are applied. A mistake should lead to a documented improvement, not another employee repeatedly fixing the same sentence. Look for Evidence Behind Security Promises Where an AI-enabled website or business integration needs independent assessment, choose a penetration testing company authorised to provide the relevant services in Ghana. The Cyber Security Authority’s licensing framework explicitly includes vulnerability assessment and penetration testing. Verify the provider’s certificate through the authority’s verification portal rather than relying on a logo in a proposal. Agree the scope, written permission, reporting process and arrangements for checking repairs. Do not authorise tests against a supplier’s infrastructure without its permission. Ask what was tested and when. The NCSC cautions that a penetration test provides assurance at a particular time, not a permanent guarantee. Security claims should describe evidence and limitations, not promise invulnerability. Calculate the Cost Beyond the Subscription Compare offers using the same workload and number of staff. Ask about setup, training, storage, support, usage limits and charges for connecting other business systems. The NCSC notes that differently priced cloud licences can include different security features. Confirm that essential protections are included in the quoted package. Record the time employees spend reviewing outputs and correcting mistakes. Faster drafting is not necessarily faster completion. Check the billing currency and renewal conditions, then ask how price changes will be communicated. Avoid committing to an annual package before a manageable trial has shown value. Require a clear support route. Identify who responds when something fails and what assistance is actually included. Plan the Exit Before Signing Ask for a demonstration of exporting records in a usable format. Check whether templates, attachments and relevant history leave with them, rather than assuming that a download contains everything. Keep an independent copy of essential business information. Agree how work will continue during an outage and who can suspend automated actions. Before renewal, compare results with the original problem. Has quotation preparation become more reliable? Are customers asking fewer clarification questions? Can employees explain and correct the output? For Ghanaian businesses, successful adoption should strengthen control rather than surrender it. The right supplier is not necessarily the one with the most impressive presentation. It is the one whose promises can be tested, whose responsibilities are clear and whose service remains worth paying for.

items.title: Santé : Ouagadougou accueille le Salon de la souveraineté sanitaire africaine du 25 au 28 novembre 2026
items.description: La 2e édition du Salon international des professionnels de santé et de l'intégration des soins (SIPSIS) se tiendra du 25 au 28 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Placée sous le thème « Défis sanitaires de la décennie 2027-2036 en Afrique : perspectives stratégiques pour la Confédération des États du Sahel dans le contexte de la souveraineté », cette rencontre ambitionne de contribuer au renforcement de la souveraineté sanitaire au Sahel et sur le continent. Face aux nombreux défis sanitaires auxquels l'Afrique est confrontée, la souveraineté sanitaire apparaît comme un enjeu stratégique majeur. Le Salon international des professionnels de santé et de l'intégration des soins (SIPSIS) entend réunir les différents acteurs et secteurs intervenant dans l'écosystème de la santé, santé humaine, animale et environnementale, autour d'objectifs communs. Adjima Combary, directeur de cabinet du ministère de la Santé, représentant le ministre, appel la population à se mobiliser pour le salon Selon Adjima Combary, directeur de cabinet du ministre de la Santé, représentant le ministre, cette rencontre vise à favoriser une mobilisation coordonnée des acteurs. « L'objectif général du SIPSIS 2026 est de contribuer à la souveraineté sanitaire de la Confédération des États du Sahel et de l'Afrique par une mobilisation coordonnée de l'écosystème de la santé », a-t-il indiqué. Pour le Burkina Faso, les retombées attendues portent notamment sur la valorisation des capacités nationales dans les différents maillons de l'écosystème sanitaire. Le représentant du ministre a ajouté que l'accueil des délégations pourrait également contribuer au dynamisme économique du pays. « Le volet SIPSIS et Jeunesse, ainsi que le manuel des métiers, devrait par ailleurs susciter des vocations et préparer une relève consciente de la diversité des professions de santé et des enjeux de souveraineté sanitaire », a-t-il déclaré. À l'échelle de la Confédération des États du Sahel (AES), le SIPSIS devrait favoriser l'identification de priorités communes, le développement de complémentarités et l'émergence de projets conjoints, notamment dans les domaines de la production et de l'approvisionnement en produits de santé. Pour l'Afrique, les attentes concernent une meilleure circulation des connaissances, la valorisation des innovations et des savoirs thérapeutiques africains, ainsi que le renforcement des partenariats entre institutions, entreprises et chercheurs. Le programme de cette deuxième édition s'articulera autour de six grandes composantes : les activités scientifiques, les expositions, les rencontres professionnelles B2B, le volet SIPSIS et Jeunesse, les visites de sites, notamment le Centre hospitalier universitaire de Pala et le barrage de Samandeni, ainsi que la Nuit de l'écosystème de santé. Par cette diversité d'activités, le SIPSIS entend se positionner comme un cadre de concertation, de partage d'expériences et de mise en relation des professionnels et des autres acteurs du secteur sanitaire, en vue de construire des réponses collectives aux défis de santé en Afrique. En guise d’information, le Salon international des professionnels de santé et de l’intégration des soins (SIPSIS) est une initiative portée par l’Association Kug-Laaga, dont la première édition s’est tenue du 27 au 30 novembre 2024 à Ouagadougou. Cette plateforme panafricaine vise à fédérer les acteurs du secteur sanitaire autour des enjeux de souveraineté sanitaire, de recherche, d’innovation et d’intégration des soins. Elle entend également promouvoir les compétences locales, encourager les partenariats et favoriser le partage d’expériences entre les pays africains. Sakinatou ZOUNDI Minute.bf

items.title: Boxe : Imane Khelif annonce ses débuts professionnels le 15 décembre à Paris
items.description: Imane Khelif va enfiler à nouveau ses gangs de boxeuse. Pour la première fois depuis sa médaille d’or historique aux JO de Paris 2024, la championne olympique algérienne va remonter sur le ring dans la capitale française. « Je vous donne rendez-vous le 15 décembre prochain à Paris pour mon premier combat professionnel », a annoncé Imane Khelif au micro d’Iconic. L'Algérienne affrontera la Néerlandaise Clarida Sarabia au Palais de la Mutualité à Paris. La championne algérienne, qui fait face à une campagne de dénigrement sur son genre depuis les championnats du monde de New Delhi en mars 2023 où elle a été disqualifiée juste avant la finale, a exprimé sa joie de retrouver la compétition et de se la boxe professionnelle. « Le ring et la boxe me manquent. Je suis née pour être boxeuse et aujourd’hui je vais retourner dans mon domaine. J’ai choisi la boxe professionnelle, et c’est le moment de le faire car le monde professionnel, c’est la vraie boxe », a-t-elle dit. Imane Khelif : « Je ne baisserai jamais les bras » Imane Khelif sait que sa nouvelle aventure ne se sera pas facile. « Je sais que c’est difficile de rester dans la boxe professionnelle et de remporter des combats, mais je fais le maximum pour bien me préparer et me concentrer pour être prête et gagner », a expliqué la boxeuse de 25 ans, avant de lancer un appel au public pour venir en masse la soutenir le 15 décembre à Paris. « J’espère que je ferai plaisir au public et ce dernier me fera l’honneur de venir dans la salle. Je vais commencer une nouvelle aventure dans la boxe professionnelle. Cela neuf mois depuis que me prépare. La préparation est différente entre la boxe amateure et professionnelle, mais je commence à m’adapter. J’espère que je vais gagner, obtenir des titres pour honorer mon pays », a-t-elle dit. Imane Khelif a enfin lancé un message clair sur son avenir et à ses détracteurs. « Je ne baisserai jamais les bras, je ne m’arrêterai jamais. Je vais continuer. Je me suis relevée pour construire une nouvelle histoire. Imene Khelif est de retour ». items.title: Banks, utilities among services put on alert against AI-enabled cyberthreats
items.description: The National Cyber Emergency Response Team (NCERT) has warned of an increased use of artificial intelligence (AI) and automated bots to carry out credential-based and coordinated cyberattacks, noting that critical infrastructure and financial services are at particular risk. NCERT, in an advisory dated Nov 5, said an increase in “AI, automated bots, botnets and agentic tools to automate reconnaissance, identify vulnerabilities, conduct credential-based attacks and launch coordinated cyberattacks” has been observed recently. “These capabilities may help threat actors and sophisticated cybercriminal groups to broaden the scale, speed and sophistication of their operations,” it added. “This advisory is relevant to all sectors/organizations. However, two sectors require particular attention,” it stressed, referring to financial services, along with operational technology (OT) and critical infrastructure. It warned banks that they could face attacks targeting core banking systems, digital banking platforms, payment systems and customer-facing applications, with potential scenarios including the disruption of online services, automated credential attacks, and manipulation of displayed account balances. In terms of critical infrastructure, NCERT warned: “Third-party service providers, connected IoT (internet of things) devices, vulnerabilities in industrial control systems and insecure remote access may expose oil and gas facilities, water utilities, power generation and distribution networks, manufacturing, transportation and other essential services. “A compromise could disrupt physical processes and critical services,” it added. NCERT cited recent incidents in Europe, where supermarket refrigerators and freezers were targeted in cyberattacks, as examples of the “physical and commercial consequences of attacks against connected operational systems”. “However, AI involvement in said incidents has not been confirmed yet,” it added. Threat indicators The advisory listed anomalies which may indicate a potential cyberattack targeting financial institutions, such as frequent automated login attempts, repeated authentication failures, and unusual application programming interface (API) requests. Abnormal transaction patterns, differences between core banking records and the displayed account balance, and unauthorised payment access were other indicators. For critical infrastructure, NCERT said changes to refinery, pipeline, grid, power generation or distribution parameters could indicate an attack, as could unexpected changes to pressure, temperature, cooling or heating control settings. Unexpected remote access sessions or changes to IoT/OT device configurations could also point towards a cyberattack. Recommendations NCERT recommended that financial institutions check their core banking security, APIs, third-party integrations, payment gateways and digital banking applications. It further urged them to use multi-factor authentication and protection against automated login attempts, while enforcing integrity checks between consumer-facing applications and core banking records. The team also suggested monitoring bot-driven attempts, potential service disruption and abnormal API activity. For utility providers, NCERT’s advice was to limit direct internet exposure and remote access and check the security of IoT assets and industrial control systems. “Enforce OT/IT network segmentation and continuously monitor access to operational systems,” it recommended. “Keep applying security updates and maintain backup operating procedures for essential processes.” NCERT also urged all organisations to check their preparedness against bot-driven AI cyberattacks, maintain incident logs and enhance arrangements for incident response, business continuity and security monitoring.

items.title: RGPH-4 : la Guinée présentée comme un modèle de référence en matière de recensement en Afrique
items.description: Sous la présidence de Mamadi Doumbouya, la Guinée voit son quatrième Recensement général de la population et de l’habitation (RGPH-4) mis en avant comme une référence sur le continent africain. Le jeudi 5 novembre 2026, à Abidjan, le Ministre du Plan, de la Coopération Internationale et du Développement, M. Ismael Nabé, a pris part au Demographic Future Dialogue 2026, organisé par l'UNFPA. Il est intervenu dans un panel de haut niveau sur les partenariats pour la résilience démographique, introduit par M. Luc GRÉGOIRE, Conseiller principal en politiques internationales. Il y siégeait aux côtés de ses homologues M. Guylain NYEMBO MBWIZYA, Vice-Premier ministre, Ministre du Plan de la RDC, et M. Paul TASONG NJUKANG, Ministre de l'Économie et de la Planification du Cameroun, ainsi que de représentants d'institutions internationales. Le Ministre NABE a présenté l'expérience guinéenne à travers les résultats du Quatrième Recensement Général de la Population et de l’Habitation (RGPH-4) : 17 521 167 habitants ; Près de 8 Guinéens sur 10 âgés de moins de 35 ans ; Un âge moyen d'environ 22 ans ; Plus de 60 % de la population vivant en milieu rural, et une majorité de femmes. Au-delà de ces résultats, il a présenté deux priorités : – Faire des données démographiques un outil d'aide à la décision publique : mieux orienter les investissements vers les besoins des populations et adapter les politiques publiques aux réalités des territoires. – Transformer le potentiel de la jeunesse en dividende démographique : investir durablement dans l'éducation, la formation professionnelle, la santé, l'entrepreneuriat et l’emploi, en cohérence avec les ambitions du programme Simandou 2040. Le Ministre Ismaël NABE a, par ailleurs, plaidé pour une mobilisation accrue de quatre types d'acteurs : Les partenaires au développement ; Les institutions financières ; Le secteur privé ; Les acteurs de la coopération Sud-Sud. Selon lui, une approche concertée et multisectorielle reste essentielle pour faire de la transition démographique une véritable opportunité de développement. «𝑼𝒏𝒆 𝒑𝒐𝒑𝒖𝒍𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒋𝒆𝒖𝒏𝒆 𝒏𝒆 𝒄𝒐𝒏𝒔𝒕𝒊𝒕𝒖𝒆 𝒑𝒂𝒔, 𝒆𝒏 𝒔𝒐𝒊, 𝒖𝒏 𝒅𝒊𝒗𝒊𝒅𝒆𝒏𝒅𝒆 𝒅𝒆́𝒎𝒐𝒈𝒓𝒂𝒑𝒉𝒊𝒒𝒖𝒆. 𝑪'𝒆𝒔𝒕 𝒖𝒏𝒆 𝒑𝒓𝒐𝒎𝒆𝒔𝒔𝒆. 𝑳𝒂 𝒄𝒐𝒏𝒄𝒓𝒆́𝒕𝒊𝒔𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒅𝒆 𝒄𝒆𝒕𝒕𝒆 𝒑𝒓𝒐𝒎𝒆𝒔𝒔𝒆 𝒆𝒏 𝒑𝒓𝒐𝒔𝒑𝒆́𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒆́ 𝒅𝒆́𝒑𝒆𝒏𝒅𝒓𝒂 𝒅𝒆 𝒍𝒂 𝒒𝒖𝒂𝒍𝒊𝒕𝒆́ 𝒅𝒆 𝒏𝒐𝒔 𝒅𝒆́𝒄𝒊𝒔𝒊𝒐𝒏𝒔, 𝒅𝒆 𝒍'𝒂𝒖𝒅𝒂𝒄𝒆 𝒅𝒆 𝒏𝒐𝒔 𝒊𝒏𝒗𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒊𝒔𝒔𝒆𝒎𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒔 𝒆𝒕 𝒅𝒆 𝒍𝒂 𝒔𝒐𝒍𝒊𝒅𝒊𝒕𝒆́ 𝒅𝒆 𝒏𝒐𝒔 𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒕𝒆𝒏𝒂𝒓𝒊𝒂𝒕𝒔. » Cette participation a également été l'occasion de saluer le partenariat historique entre la Guinée et l'UNFPA, notamment dans les domaines du recensement, de la santé maternelle et reproductive, de l'autonomisation des femmes et du renforcement du système statistique national. En partageant son expérience au Dialogue sur l'avenir démographique à Abidjan, la Guinée réaffirme son ambition : ne pas seulement connaître sa population, mais faire de son potentiel humain le moteur de sa transformation économique et sociale. Nollywood actor Diewait Ikpechukwu dies at 71
items.description: Veteran Nollywood actor Diewait Ikpechukwu has died at the age of 71, bringing to an end a career that spanned more than two decades in the Nigerian film industry. The actor reportedly died on Thursday, November 5, 2026, with the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN) confirming his passing on Friday, November 6. AGN National President, Alhaji Abubakar Sanusi Yakubu, announced the death in a tribute, describing Ikpechukwu as another legend whose memories would remain with the industry. Ikpechukwu was particularly recognised for his portrayal of traditional rulers and other authoritative characters in Nollywood productions. His performances in films such as Evil Men , alongside veteran actor Pete Edochie, as well as Python King , The Guilty and Omera , earned him recognition among audiences. Beyond his work on screen, he played an active role in the Actors Guild of Nigeria, serving as chairman of its Enugu State chapter, where he supported and mentored emerging actors. His journey into entertainment, however, was not limited to acting. Before establishing himself in Nollywood, Ikpechukwu was an accomplished footballer in the 1970s and reportedly earned an invitation to join Nigeria’s national team, then known as the Green Eagles. He later ventured into radio broadcasting, working as a sports commentator before pursuing a career in film. Ikpechukwu is survived by his wife, Gloria, children and grandchildren, who join colleagues, friends and fans in mourning his passing. His death marks another loss for Nollywood, particularly among the generation of actors whose performances helped shape the Nigerian film industry.

items.title: Mining Reforms Must Protect Jobs, Investment and Community Interests — Ghana Chamber of Mines
items.description: The Ghana Chamber of Mines has called for sustained dialogue and careful consideration of the economic implications of ongoing mining sector reforms, stressing that efforts to deepen Ghanaian participation must also safeguard employment, investment and the industry’s long-term competitiveness. The Chamber’s Chief Operating Officer, Ahmed Dasana Nantogmah, said recent concerns expressed by mineworkers and host communities highlighted the importance of consultation and a balanced approach to mining policy and regulatory decisions. His comments follow protests by mineworkers at Akyem Abirem over the directive to transition certain mining operations from owner mining to contract mining. The workers have raised concerns about potential implications for job security, wages, benefits and existing conditions of service. Mr. Nantogmah acknowledged government’s commitment to strengthening local participation in the mining industry, describing it as an important national objective that the Chamber supports. “Greater Ghanaian participation in mining is an objective we all share. However, the approach must protect existing jobs, maintain safety and operational efficiency, and ensure that the industry remains competitive enough to sustain investment and create new opportunities,” he said. He emphasised that significant changes to established mining operating models require meaningful consultation among regulators, mining companies, employees and other stakeholders to ensure that policy objectives are achieved without unintended economic consequences. Commenting on the ongoing discussions surrounding the renewal of Gold Fields Ghana’s Tarkwa mining leases, Mr. Nantogmah acknowledged the expectations of host communities for greater and more visible benefits from mineral development. “Mining communities must see tangible improvements in their livelihoods. Equally, investors must have confidence that their rights and obligations will be administered fairly and consistently. These objectives are not mutually exclusive,” he stated. He stressed the importance of constructive engagement with traditional authorities and other stakeholders, while ensuring that decisions concerning mineral rights are guided by transparent, predictable and lawful procedures. Mr. Nantogmah also noted the recent regulatory developments involving Adamus Resources and Northern Ashanti Mines, emphasising the importance of continued engagement in addressing such matters. He acknowledged the responsibility of the Minerals Commission and the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources to ensure compliance with mining laws, while encouraging dialogue, due process and mutual understanding in resolving regulatory concerns in the interest of sustaining investor confidence and protecting Ghana’s mining industry. The COO further pointed to recent operational and financial results announced by Galiano Gold and AngloGold Ashanti as indications of the industry’s capacity to sustain production and pursue further investment opportunities. He noted that realising this potential requires a stable operating environment, access to capital and a competitive fiscal and regulatory framework. “Our collective objective should be to develop mining policies that secure fair revenues for the State, expand opportunities for Ghanaian businesses, protect jobs and deliver lasting benefits to communities, while encouraging the investments needed to sustain future mineral production,” he said. Mr. Nantogmah reaffirmed the Chamber’s commitment to working constructively with government, regulators, organised labour, traditional authorities and other stakeholders to strengthen Ghana’s position as a competitive and responsible mining investment destination.

items.title: The Education a STEM Major Needs
items.description: This is an edition of the Books Briefing, our editors’ weekly guide to the best in books. Sign up for it here. In 2014, I graduated from college with a dubious degree: I majored in English, a discipline that, in a time of growing STEM mania, was widely considered a relic of questionable value. At the end of my studies, my adviser asked me what I’d taken away from the program. My answer: how to think. I had spent enough time examining the minds of brilliant others—learning how they chose words, built characters, and developed ideas—to feel some mastery over my own. In a new Atlantic essay , Joshua Bennett, a literature professor at MIT, makes the case that such an education should be foundational for all students, including and perhaps especially those focusing on science. First, here are six new stories from The Atlantic ’s Books section: Six books you should read twice He was hugely influential. He also had a foolish streak. Forget grit. The golden age of hockey literature What if the apocalypse is already here? “The Toll,” a poem by Forrest Gander Bennett’s students have grown up in a society defined by rapid technological growth; some of them likely dream of building a world we can’t imagine today, especially now that new AI technologies are pushing the frontier of the possible. At the same time, the state of the humanities has become even more fragile than it was during my undergraduate career. Humanities departments across the country are being squeezed or shut down entirely. Too many students have never been assigned the once-standard task of reading a whole book. The number of undergraduate humanities degrees awarded by American universities in 2025 was nearly a third lower than it was in 2012, although the decline might be approaching a plateau. That crisis is part of what’s driving Bennett and some of his colleagues to design a Great Books course for MIT, the kind of sweeping introduction to canonical, time-tested literature and philosophy that helps anchor many liberal-arts educations. Given the students he’s working with, Bennett’s program will focus on “the history, poetics, and philosophy of science.” A solid grounding in the humanities, he argues, is essential to the intellectual development of future scientists, in part because it can help them “identify irreplaceable ideas during a time of accelerated change.” The possibility of an imminent techno-utopia, in which work is automated and life is easy—or, conversely, a tech-driven apocalypse, in which human inventions come to subjugate humanity—makes it ever more important to teach students how to engage deeply with the age-old query: What is life for? Studying the plays of the ancient Greeks or the logical puzzles of Kant won’t, of course, provide a single answer. But doing so can help teach students how to think about the problem—to wonder, What is the meaning of life? as well as, What distinguishes a thoughtful idea from a shallow truism? To ask more questions, and to pursue the answers with rigor, is to open more routes toward meaning. Bennett’s “irreplaceable ideas” are not formulas to memorize; they’re vigorous, adaptable entities. You cannot learn, once and for all, what they mean. You can only build the habit of thinking about them for yourself. Illustration by The Atlantic . Source: Getty. The Time Is Right for a ‘Great Books’ Revival By Joshua Bennett To build a better world in the age of AI, students need grounding in indispensable ideas. Read the full article. What to Read The Perfectionists , by Simon Winchester The Perfectionists dramatically explores the history of engineers figuring out how to manufacture things—mostly out of metal, glass and other hard materials—into exacting shapes and sizes, making possible our world of cars, jet engines, and microprocessor chips. The story begins, and is intimately bound up, with the Industrial Revolution. John Wilkinson, one of the fathers of precision engineering, devised snug-fitting cylinders for James Watt’s steam engine, and the early days of the discipline are similarly full of delightfully specific historical objects: pulleys made for British naval ships, for example, and the fiddly bits of flintlock muskets. But as Winchester steps through the great advancements that pushed this school of engineering to new extremes, he makes clear that we now rely on machines to achieve a perfection unattainable by people, and that this comes with hefty stakes. An improperly machined oil pipe, for instance, caused catastrophic engine failure on a 2010 Qantas flight because it was “about half a millimeter too thin,” he writes. (Thanks to an experienced crew, everyone on board survived.) Perhaps, he suggests, a deeper respect for imperfect human craftsmanship might live alongside our reverence for mechanical technique. — Chelsea Leu From our list: Eight books that explain how the world works Out Next Week 📚 The Land of Tears and Hope: The Ukrainian Story , by Illia Ponomarenko 📚 Vocal Break: On Women, Music, and Power , by Lauren Elkin 📚 No Such Thing as Monday: A Novel , by Siân Hughes Your Weekend Read Ian Loring Shiver and Minnie Park for The Atlantic The Rise of the Tallboy Is a Sign of the Times By Megan Garber Say you’re at a football game (fun!), in large part for the food (correct!). You have spent your time at the stadium successfully curating an alfresco fine-dining experience: the pregame amuse-bouche (popcorn, maybe, with a swirl of let’s-agree-to-call-it-butter), the first-quarter aperitif (a frosty can of beer), the second-quarter appetizer (a plate of fries, doused with ketchup), the third-quarter entrée (nachos, obviously, washed down with a second beer). It’s now the fourth quarter, and although the game has gone as planned (probably? you haven’t been paying tons of attention), your dessert course has not. items.title: Petrol price down by Rs6.59 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs4.25 in fifth straight reduction
items.description: The government on Friday once again decreased the price of petrol by Rs6.59 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.25, in the fifth consecutive cut in fuel prices. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs346 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs378. The prices are applicable from Nov 7 (Saturday) to Nov 10 (Tuesday) due to a public holiday on Nov 9, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra). The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end. Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). Rise in fuel prices The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months. On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: COCOBOD relaunches free fertilizer programme with new monitoring platform to boost farmer incomes
items.description: The government has relaunched the Free Fertilizer and Agro-Input Programme for cocoa farmers under a major intervention to restore productivity, improve farmer incomes, and reset the cocoa sector. The program is a policy shift from a 50-per cent subsidy to free fertilizer distribution to farmers, which the Ghana Cocoa Board says represents a total reset of how government intends to support farmers and increase cocoa production. The relaunch of the program has seen the procurement of over 3.5 million bags of granular fertilizer for distribution to cocoa farmers nationwide. Approximately 1.2 million bags have already been delivered to farmers as a new digital platform has been developed to strengthen accountability and ensure fair distribution. Speaking at the event, Chief Executive Officer of COCOBOD, Dr. Randy Abbey, described the intervention as a decisive declaration that government, through COCOBOD, is fully committed to relieving the financial burdens of farmers. He explained the initiative also seeks to restore maximum productivity to the soil and secure the golden future of the cocoa sector. “We are removing financial barriers to high yields. Free fertilizer is not a handout; it is an investment in farmers, in the soil, and in the foreign exchange earnings of this republic,” Dr. Abbey said. The relaunch held at Sefwi Wiawso under the theme: “ Cocoa Sector Reset: Free Fertilizer for Increased Productivity and Improved Farmer Income ,” brought together government officials, traditional leaders, farmers, and other stakeholders in the cocoa value chain. Farmers with mature and productive cocoa plantations in designated operational district areas are expected to receive fertilizer, whether granular or liquid, as well as insecticides and fungicides. The COCOBOD will also supply free pneumatic and motorized sprayers to farmers. Dr. Abbey noted that the board is fully aware of the challenges that plagued previous free distribution systems, highlighting that the good intentions of the state to revamp the sector were rather undermined by diversion, smuggling, favouritism, and unfair distribution. “Inputs meant for genuine farmers ended up in open markets across the borders and on the farms of the well-connected, while smallholder farmers at the end of the line went home empty-handed,” he noted. The COCOBOD is rolling out a new digital system to track every input taken from the warehouses to farms to ensure accountability and prevent abuse of the reintroduced initiative. According to the COCOBOD boss, every beneficiary must register and have their farms marked and captured on the Digital Cocoa Management System (CMS). The identity of every farmer will be verified at the point of collection through the national identification card or by biometric data. “This time, we have built the entire distribution around a new digital distribution system that follows every bag or litre of input from the warehouse to the farm. No one can collect the fertilizer and the agro-inputs in another person’s name, and no ghost farmer names can appear on the list,” Dr. Abbey said. He added that the system calculates each farmer’s entitlement automatically based on the marked size and condition of the farm, and therefore, officers at distribution points cannot add or deduct from the allocation. Dr. Abbey cautioned smugglers and saboteurs, stressing that any officer, buyer, or individual found diverting or selling the distribution inputs will face the full rigours of the law. The cocoa industry continues to face significant challenges, including declining productivity, ageing and unproductive farms, rising production costs, labour constraints, soil fertility challenges, persistent threats of capsid pests and swollen shoot virus disease, and the increasing effects of climate variability. Highlighting the importance of cocoa to the country’s economy, Board Chairman of the COCOBOD, Dr. Samuel Ofosu-Ampofo, noted that these challenges require deliberate, coordinated and sustained interventions. He noted that the distribution of the fertilizers is in line with the government’s commitment to addressing the challenges confronting the cocoa value chain. “We cannot expect increased national cocoa production without investing adequately in the farms and supporting the farmers who cultivate them. Equally, we cannot achieve sustainable productivity if we do not address the underlying challenges of soil fertility, pest and disease management, access to improved planting material and effective extension services,” he said. Additionally, the COCOBOD says 1.8 million litres of liquid fertilizer, 2.3 million litres of insecticide, and 1.5 million kilograms of fungicide have been purchased for cocoa farmers across the country. Dr. Ofosu-Ampofo said that the government has unprecedentedly supplied about 27,000 new spray machines in a single year, bringing the total number of spray machines available to about 67,000. To complement the supply of sprayers and chemicals, he also noted that approximately 5.7 million litres of pre-mixed fuel have been supplied to cocoa farmers to support the mechanical application of liquid fertilizer and insecticides. The board and management of COCOBOD say they remain committed to ensuring a sustainable cocoa economy that provides optimal benefits to farmers, sustains profitable and integrated value chains, as well as promotes environmental resilience and social inclusion.

items.title: Farmers urged to enroll in insurance policies to protect investments against El Niño impacts
items.description: The recent climatic phenomenon, El Niño, is prompting the urgency for farmers to take immediate steps to seek insurance protection for their investments. Despite the rollout of insurance policies, including the Ghana Agriculture Insurance Pool, for the agricultural value chain, many farmers fail to leverage the avenues to mitigate financial hardship brought about by unpredictable weather conditions and crop diseases. The Chartered Insurance Institute of Ghana is pushing for farmers to safeguard their investment now against the vagaries of the harsh weather as the world is predicted to further heat up in the ensuing years. Weather and climate experts predict intense weather conditions in the coming years, exposing uninsured farmers to more threats of loss. Despite a pool of insurance policies, farmers continue to lose out on their benefits. The insurers are moving to strengthen insurance products for the agriculture sector to rope in more farmers to safeguard their investments. Speaking at the annual conference of the Chartered Insurance Institute of Ghana in Kumasi, Chairman of the Insurance Awareness Coordinators Group, Wilson Teye, highlighted challenges confronting the rollout and uptake of the policies by farmers. “We haven’t had mechanized agriculture. We depend completely on the vagaries of the weather and that is a problem. Even some of our methods, such as deliberately setting fires on farms, are issues. There is also the challenge of bring all the farmers together to understand and appreciate the need for insurance. But regardless, we have brought this to the forefront and are addressing agricultural insurance,” he said. Agricultural insurance provides protection to key stakeholders in the agricultural production value chain in the event of crop failure ad livestock mortality due to both natural phenomena and human-induced activities. President of the Chartered Insurance Institute of Ghana, Solomon Nii Amah-Kai Lartey, says the time is now for vulnerable large- and small-scale farmers to secure their produce. “Make sure you have your insurance now. There is parametric insurance, which does need much assessment after a loss. Once the parameters are triggered, a claim can be made. With the emergence of El Niño, people should get insured now,” he said. Mr. Amah-Kai also disclosed that farmers and other stakeholders along the agriculture value chain can leverage the dedicated insurance pool for subsidized products. “The Ghana Agriculture Insurance Pool is available for agriculture stakeholders. This pool is there to ensure that agric insurance premiums are subsidized for people to be able to buy insurance,” he said. Deputy Commissioner of Insurance, Bernard Ohemeng Baah, emphasized the importance of insurance for agriculture as he revealed that the National Insurance Commission is in its concluding stages to roll out subsidized agriculture insurance for smallholder farmers. “Because we don’t have data, the price of insurance for farmers tends to be really high. So, many of them don’t patronize it. We are employing innovative approaches to deliver insurance to farmers at a low cost. This will help protect Ghana’s food basket and also ensure that families that depend on agriculture are not exposed to the shocks of the weather,” he said. Closing the Insurance Gap The AGM and educational conference of the insurers, held on the theme: “ Closing the Gap: From Awareness to Action in Building an Adaptive Insurance Industry ,” assembled professional stakeholders in the sector to leverage the opportunity in building a resilient insurance industry. Ghana’s insurance industry, despite making considerable gains, is still confronted with significant gaps between public awareness, insurance ownership, and effective financial protection. In 2024, Ghana’s insurance penetration stood at approximately 1.0 per cent of the gross domestic product (GDP). The International Financial Reporting Standards report 0.63 per cent associated with insurance service revenue. But insurers only paid approximately 3.6 billion cedis in claims during 2024. Mr. Nii Amah-Kai noted that the challenge must extend beyond just raising awareness but must extend insurance protection to more people and businesses and also to ensure that the experience of purchasing and using insurance justifies the public’s confidence in the insurance cover. “We need to make sure that the awareness we are creating is translating into real insurance take-up. This conference seeks to find answers to whether or not the awareness is properly done and how it is benefiting the Ghanaian people,” he said. Mr. Wilson Teye says people’s trust and confidence must be heightened to increase their enrolment in insurance policy avenues. “The bedrock of insurance is payment of claims. If people do not trust that their claims will be paid and on time, they naturally wouldn’t want their money buying insurance. The objective is to address the mistrust and get regulatory intervention,” he said. As part of the annual activities, the association also visited the T.I. Ahmadiyya SHS in Kumasi to sensitize students on the job prospects in pursuing study programmes in insurance and actuarial science. The association also invested in the digital infrastructure of the school with the donation of printers and learning projectors to aid academic work, while also providing some souvenirs from member insurance companies.
